title: Bowling Game Scorer
spec: A single word entry function `score(rolls)` takes a list of integers representing pins knocked down. It must iterate through ten frames. A strike is ten pins on the first roll, advancing immediately to the next frame and adding the next two rolls as a bonus. A spare is ten pins over two rolls, adding the next roll as a bonus. Open frames just sum the two rolls. The tenth frame allows up to three rolls if a strike or spare is rolled. If the list contains too few or too many rolls for a valid game, return a negative one. Output the final integer score. Example: a list of twelve tens outputs three hundred.

title: Poker Hand Evaluator
spec: A single word entry function `evaluate(hand)` takes a list of five strings, each representing a card with a rank and suit. It must parse the rank and suit separately. Ranks are two through nine, ten, jack, queen, king, and ace. It must count the frequencies of each rank and suit. A flush is five cards of the same suit. A straight is five consecutive ranks. The function must determine the highest combination: straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, one pair, or high card. Return an integer from one for high card up to nine for straight flush. Example: a list of five hearts in consecutive order returns nine.

title: Employee Payroll Processor
spec: A single word entry function `payroll(record)` takes a tuple of hourly rate, hours worked, and an exemption status boolean. First, it calculates regular pay for up to forty hours. Any hours over forty earn time and a half, unless the exemption status is true, in which case all hours are paid at the regular rate. Next, calculate gross pay. A flat union dues deduction of twenty is subtracted if gross pay exceeds two hundred. Then, apply a progressive tax rate: zero percent for the first five hundred, ten percent for the next five hundred, and twenty percent for anything above one thousand. Return the final net pay rounded to two decimals. Example: twenty, forty five, false returns seven hundred fifty six.

title: Password Strength Analyzer
spec: A single word entry function `analyze(password)` takes a string and evaluates its security. First, check if the length is at least twelve characters, deducting points if shorter. Add a point if it has uppercase letters and another for lowercase letters. Add a point for containing numbers and one for special symbols. Deduct two points if the password consists entirely of numbers or entirely of letters. Check for repeating sequences of three or more identical characters and deduct a point if found. Finally, ensure the score is bounded between zero and five. Return the final integer score. Example: an all lowercase word of length six returns zero.

title: Tennis Match Scorer
spec: A single word entry function `tally(points)` takes a list of strings where each string is either player one or player two, representing who won the point. The score starts at zero for both. Points translate to fifteen, thirty, and forty. If both players reach forty, the state becomes deuce. From deuce, a player must score twice in a row to win; one point gives them the advantage, and losing the next returns it to deuce. Once a player wins a game, reset the points and increment their game count. The first to win six games with a margin of two wins the set. Return a tuple of the final game counts. Example: twenty four consecutive wins for player one returns six and zero.

title: Library Fine Calculator
spec: A single word entry function `fines(days)` takes an integer representing the number of days a book is overdue. The first three days are a grace period with no charge. Days four through ten incur a daily fee of fifty cents. Days eleven through twenty incur a fee of one dollar per day. Any days beyond twenty incur a two dollar daily fee. If the total days exceed thirty, add a flat replacement fee of twenty dollars. The maximum fine, excluding the replacement fee, is capped at fifteen dollars. Compute the total amount and return it as a floating point number. Example: returning a book five days late yields one point zero.

title: Flight Pricing Engine
spec: A single word entry function `quote(details)` takes a tuple of base fare, days until departure, baggage count, and a loyalty tier string. First, apply a time discount: if booked more than thirty days in advance, reduce the base fare by ten percent. If booked within seven days, add a twenty percent premium. Next, add baggage fees: the first bag is twenty five, the second is forty, and any additional bags are fifty each. If the loyalty tier is gold, waive the first bag fee. If the loyalty tier is platinum, waive the first two bag fees and apply a five percent discount to the total. Return the final price rounded to the nearest integer. Example: two hundred, forty, one, plain returns two hundred five.

title: Date String Validator
spec: A single word entry function `validate(date)` takes a string in day month year format separated by hyphens. First, split the string into three components and ensure they are all numeric. Extract the year and check if it is between nineteen hundred and twenty one hundred. Determine if the year is a leap year, which occurs every four years but not on centuries unless divisible by four hundred. Check the month is between one and twelve. Assign the maximum days for the month, accounting for february in a leap year. Ensure the day is between one and the maximum days for that month. Return a boolean indicating if the date is valid. Example: twenty nine hyphen zero two hyphen two thousand returns true.

title: Sudoku Board Checker
spec: A single word entry function `check(board)` takes a list of nine lists, each with nine integers from zero to nine, where zero is an empty cell. First, verify the board has exactly nine rows and nine columns. Then iterate through each row to ensure no non zero duplicates exist. Do the same for each of the nine columns. Next, divide the board into nine three by three subgrids and check each for duplicate numbers. Keep track of how many zeros remain on the board. If the board has duplicates, return negative one. If it is valid but incomplete, return zero. If valid and complete, return one. Example: a completely filled valid board returns one.

title: Vending Machine Change
spec: A single word entry function `vend(payment)` takes a tuple of price and amount given in cents. First, verify the amount given is greater than or equal to the price. Calculate the total change required. Define the available coin denominations as quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies. Iterate through the denominations from largest to smallest. For each coin, determine the maximum number that can be used to make change. Subtract that value from the remaining change. Keep a tally of each coin type used. Return a tuple of four integers representing the counts of quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies. Example: price fifty and amount one hundred returns two, zero, zero, zero.

title: Simple Markdown Parser
spec: A single word entry function `parse(lines)` takes a list of strings representing markdown text. Iterate through each line. If a line starts with a hash and a space, convert it to a level one heading. If it starts with two hashes and a space, make it a level two heading. If a line starts with an asterisk and a space, treat it as an unordered list item. Blank lines should close any open lists. Wrap any other lines in paragraph tags. Replace occurrences of double asterisks around text with bold tags. Return a single joined string of the resulting html. Example: a line with a hash and hello becomes an h one tag wrapping hello.

title: Progressive Tax Calculator
spec: A single word entry function `tax(income)` takes an integer representing annual income. First, deduct a standard allowance of twelve thousand. If the remaining income is zero or less, the tax is zero. For the next twenty thousand, apply a ten percent rate. For the subsequent forty thousand, apply a twenty percent rate. Any income above this threshold is taxed at thirty percent. Add a flat surcharge of five hundred if the original income exceeds one hundred thousand. Return the total computed tax as a rounded integer. Example: fifteen thousand returns three hundred.

title: IPv4 Address Validator
spec: A single word entry function `verify(address)` takes a string representing a network address. First, split the string by periods and verify there are exactly four segments. Loop through each segment and check if it consists only of digits. Reject any segment that starts with a zero unless it is a single zero. Convert each segment to an integer and ensure it falls between zero and two hundred fifty five inclusive. Identify if the address is a loopback starting with one two seven. Finally, identify if it is a multicast address starting with two two four or higher. Return a string describing the address type or invalid. Example: one period one period one period one returns valid.

title: URL Component Extractor
spec: A single word entry function `extract(url)` takes a string representing a web address. First, find the protocol by looking for the colon slash slash delimiter, defaulting to http if missing. Next, isolate the domain name by finding the next slash or the end of the string. Check if the domain contains a port number separated by a colon, and separate it if so. Find the path, which is everything from the first single slash up to a question mark. Finally, extract the query string after the question mark and split it by ampersands into a list of key value pairs. Return a tuple of protocol, domain, port, path, and the list of pairs. Example: a basic secure site returns https, domain, empty port, slash, and empty list.

title: E-commerce Cart Checkout
spec: A single word entry function `checkout(cart)` takes a list of tuples containing item price, quantity, and a category string. Iterate through the items to compute the raw subtotal. Apply a bulk discount of ten percent to any item where the quantity is five or more. Sum the discounted prices to get a new subtotal. If the category is electronics, apply a flat environmental fee of five. If the subtotal is over fifty, shipping is free; otherwise add ten for shipping. Finally, calculate a sales tax of eight percent on the items but not on the shipping or fees. Return the final total as a float. Example: one electronics item at ten returns twenty five point eight.

title: Elevator Dispatch Logic
spec: A single word entry function `dispatch(requests)` takes a list of integer floor requests. The elevator starts at floor zero. First, filter out any invalid requests below zero or above fifty. Sort the remaining requests based on proximity to the current floor. Move the elevator to the closest requested floor and record the movement. If multiple floors are equally close, prefer moving upwards. After reaching a floor, remove it from the pending list and add a three second door opening penalty. Keep a running tally of total floors traveled and penalty times. Return the total time taken assuming one second per floor. Example: requests for three and five return eleven.

title: Tic Tac Toe Evaluator
spec: A single word entry function `evaluate(grid)` takes a list of three strings, each containing three characters of either x, o, or dot. First, verify the grid size is correct. Count the number of x and o characters to ensure players took turns; the difference must be zero or one. Check all three rows for a matching set of three identical player characters. Check all three columns for a matching set. Check both diagonals for a win. If both x and o have a winning line, return invalid. If one player wins, return their character. If the board is full with no winner, return draw. Otherwise return pending. Example: a row of three x characters returns x.

title: Roman Numeral Decoder
spec: A single word entry function `decode(numeral)` takes a string representing a roman numeral. Define the values for each letter from one for i up to one thousand for m. Iterate through the string character by character. For each character, look up its integer value. Compare this value to the value of the next character in the string. If the current value is less than the next value, subtract it from the running total, representing subtractive notation like four or nine. Otherwise, add the value to the total. Keep track of repeated characters to reject invalid strings with four consecutive identical letters. Return the integer result or zero if invalid. Example: x i v returns fourteen.

title: Cellular Automata Step
spec: A single word entry function `step(grid)` takes a list of lists of booleans representing a grid of cells. Create a new empty grid of the same dimensions. Iterate over every row and column index. For each cell, count the number of true neighbors in all eight directions, making sure to check grid boundaries so as not to index out of bounds. If the current cell is true and has two or three neighbors, it stays true in the new grid. If it has fewer than two or more than three, it becomes false. If a false cell has exactly three neighbors, it becomes true. Return the new grid. Example: a three by three grid with a vertical line of trues returns a horizontal line.

title: Credit Card Validator
spec: A single word entry function `luhn(card)` takes a string representing a credit card number. First, strip any spaces or hyphens from the input. Verify the remaining string is entirely numeric and between thirteen and nineteen digits long. Reverse the digits to process them from right to left. Double the value of every second digit. If the doubled value is greater than nine, subtract nine from it. Sum all the digits, both the unmodified ones and the adjusted doubled ones. If the total sum modulo ten is zero, the card is valid. Identify the network: a leading four is visa, and a five is mastercard. Return a tuple of a boolean and the network string. Example: a valid visa string returns true and visa.

title: Morse Code Translator
spec: A single word entry function `translate(message)` takes a string of text to convert to morse code. Define an alphabet mapping to dots and dashes. First, convert the input string to uppercase. Iterate through each character in the message. If the character is a letter or number, append its morse equivalent to a list. If the character is a space, append a special word separator like a slash. Ignore any punctuation or unknown characters. Join the list into a final string, using a single space to separate each letter code. Ensure there are no trailing spaces. Return the coded string. Example: the word hi returns four dots space two dots.

title: Recipe Scaling Utility
spec: A single word entry function `scale(recipe)` takes a tuple containing a list of ingredient amounts, a list of units, and a target multiplier float. Loop through the amounts and multiply each by the target factor. Check the new amount and its corresponding unit. If a unit is teaspoons and the new amount exceeds three, convert it to tablespoons. If tablespoons exceed sixteen, convert to cups. Round all final amounts to two decimal places. If an amount is less than one quarter, clamp it to zero point two five for practicality. Return a list of tuples containing the adjusted amounts and units. Example: two teaspoons doubled returns one tablespoon and one teaspoon left over.

title: Commuter Fare Calculator
spec: A single word entry function `fare(journey)` takes a tuple of distance in miles, peak hour boolean, and passenger age. The base fare is calculated at twenty cents per mile. If the passenger is under twelve, apply a fifty percent discount. If the passenger is over sixty five, apply a thirty percent discount. If the journey occurs during peak hours, add a flat surcharge of two dollars and fifty cents. If the distance is over fifty miles, apply a long distance discount of ten percent to the mileage portion before surcharges. Cap the final fare at a maximum of thirty dollars. Return the computed fare rounded to two decimals. Example: ten miles off peak adult returns two.

title: Server Log Analyzer
spec: A single word entry function `analyze(logs)` takes a list of strings representing log entries. Each entry contains a timestamp, an error level, and a message separated by pipes. Initialize counters for info, warning, and error levels. Loop through each string and split it by the pipe character. Skip any malformed lines that do not have exactly three parts. Trim whitespace from the error level and increment the corresponding counter. If an error message contains the word timeout, add it to a separate critical list. Return a tuple containing the three counters and the list of critical messages. Example: three well formed info logs return three, zero, zero, and an empty list.

title: Warehouse Restock Predictor
spec: A single word entry function `predict(stock)` takes a tuple of current inventory count, daily usage rate, lead time in days, and safety stock level. First, calculate the expected consumption during the lead time by multiplying usage by lead time. Determine the reorder point by adding the expected consumption to the safety stock. If the current inventory is greater than the reorder point, no action is needed, return zero. If the inventory is lower, calculate the deficit. Determine the minimum order quantity, which is fixed at one hundred units. Round the deficit up to the nearest multiple of the minimum order quantity. Return the number of units to order. Example: fifty current and fifty usage returns a multiple of one hundred.

title: Order Book Matching Engine
spec: Write a function `match(orders)` that processes a list of stock market orders where each order is a tuple of type, price, and quantity. The function must maintain separate lists for buy orders and sell orders. Buy orders must be sorted descending by price, and sell orders sorted ascending by price. For each incoming order, attempt to execute a trade if the highest buy price is greater than or equal to the lowest sell price. If an exact match occurs, remove both orders or reduce their quantities accordingly. Keep track of all executed trades as tuples of price and quantity. Return a list of all executed trades in the order they occurred. For example, given an incoming buy for ten at fifty and a sell for five at forty, the output should include a trade of five at fifty.

title: Calendar Meeting Scheduler
spec: Create a function `schedule(meetings)` that takes a list of meeting requests, each defined by a start time, end time, and priority level. The goal is to find the maximum number of non-overlapping high priority meetings. First, filter out any meetings that last longer than four hours or end after evening hours. Next, sort the remaining meetings by their end times to prepare for a greedy scheduling approach. Iterate through the sorted list, adding a meeting to the accepted list only if its start time is strictly after the end time of the last accepted meeting. If a conflict occurs, prefer a meeting with a higher priority if it fits within the same time window without displacing earlier meetings. Return the start and end times of the finalized schedule. Given a list of morning and afternoon overlaps, it should output only the non-conflicting sequence.

title: Word Wrapping Pagination
spec: Implement `paginate(text)` to format a long string of raw text into pages with strict line length limits. The algorithm must first split the raw text into individual words, discarding extra spaces. Construct lines by appending words until the maximum width of eighty characters is reached, taking care to not split words across lines. If a single word exceeds the line length, it must be forcefully broken with a hyphen. Group the constructed lines into pages of exactly twenty five lines each. Add a page number at the bottom center of each page block. Return a list of strings representing the fully formatted pages. An input of a thousand words should return a list of several formatted page strings with numbering.

title: Infix Math Evaluator
spec: Develop an evaluator `calculate(expression)` that parses and computes the result of a mathematical string containing numbers, parenthesis, addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Use the shunting yard algorithm to first convert the infix string into a postfix token list. Maintain an operator stack and check precedence rules to ensure multiplication and division are processed before addition and subtraction. Once the postfix list is built, iterate through it using a separate evaluation stack to compute the final numerical result. Handle division by zero by returning a plain string indicating a math error. Given a string with nested parenthesis and mixed operators, it should return the correct integer or float evaluation.

title: Huffman Compression Tree
spec: Write a function `compress(text)` that builds a Huffman coding tree for a given string and returns the encoded binary representation. First, calculate the frequency of every character in the text and create a leaf node for each. Insert all nodes into a priority queue ordered by frequency. Repeatedly extract the two nodes with the lowest frequencies, create a new parent node combining their counts, and reinsert it until only one root node remains. Traverse the resulting tree to assign a binary string to each character, using zero for left branches and one for right branches. Finally, replace each character in the original string with its binary code. An input of a repetitive string should return the compressed binary sequence.

title: Package Dependency Resolver
spec: Design a function `resolve(packages)` that determines the installation order for software packages based on their dependencies. The input is a list of tuples containing a package name and a list of its required packages. Build a directed graph representing these relationships and compute the in-degree for every node. Use a queue to perform a topological sort, starting with packages that have zero dependencies. As each package is processed, decrement the in-degree of its neighbors and add them to the queue if they reach zero. If the final sorted list length does not match the total number of unique packages, detect a circular dependency and return an empty list. Given a valid set of interrelated packages, return the sequential list of names for installation.

title: Intersection Traffic Simulator
spec: Provide a simulator `simulate(cars)` that models traffic flowing through a four-way intersection over time. The input is a list of arrival times and directions for incoming vehicles. Maintain four separate queues for north, south, east, and west lanes. The traffic light operates on a fixed cycle, granting green lights to north and south for thirty seconds, then switching to east and west for thirty seconds. For each second of the simulation, check the current light phase and remove one car from the front of the corresponding active queues if vehicles are waiting. Record the wait time for every departed car. Return the average wait time across all cars once the queues are completely empty. An input of staggered arrivals should yield the average delay as a float.

title: Block Checksum Generator
spec: Create a hashing function `checksum(message)` that computes a secure checksum integer for a given string. Convert the string into its corresponding byte values and pad the sequence with zeros until its length is a multiple of sixty four. Break the padded data into blocks of exactly sixteen bytes. Initialize a starting hash integer. For each block, perform a bitwise exclusive or operation with the current hash, then apply a bitwise left shift by three positions. To add diffusion, multiply the result by a large prime number and constrain it to a thirty two bit integer using modulo arithmetic. Return the final accumulated integer hash. A short message should produce a large pseudo random number.

title: Memory Garbage Collector
spec: Implement a function `collect(memory)` that simulates a mark and sweep garbage collection algorithm. The input is a list of object allocations, where each object is a tuple of its unique identifier, its size, and a list of referenced object identifiers. A separate root list determines the starting points for reachable objects. During the mark phase, traverse the references starting from the roots using a stack, flagging every visited object as reachable. During the sweep phase, iterate through all allocated objects and identify those without the reachable flag. Sum the sizes of all unflagged objects to determine the total freed memory and remove them from the heap. Return a tuple of the total bytes freed and a list of the remaining active identifiers. Given a graph with isolated cycles, it should successfully reclaim them.

title: Arcade Collision Engine
spec: Write a function `detect(frames)` that processes a sequence of game state frames to find laser collisions with enemy ships. Each frame contains a list of player laser coordinates and a list of enemy bounding boxes. For every laser in a frame, check if its horizontal and vertical position falls within the boundaries of any active enemy box. If a collision is detected, mark the enemy as destroyed and remove the laser from the active list. Additionally, check if any surviving enemies have descended below the player base threshold, triggering an immediate game over status. Return a list of destroyed enemy coordinates and the final game state string. Given a sequence of advancing enemies and fired lasers, it should output the hits and survival status.

title: Adaptive Cache Manager
spec: Create a manager `cache(requests)` that simulates a hybrid memory cache using both recent usage and frequency data. The cache has a maximum capacity of ten items. When a new item is requested, check if it already exists in the cache and increment its hit counter if so. If the item is missing and the cache is full, identify the eviction candidate by finding the item with the lowest hit count. In the event of a tie between multiple items with the same lowest frequency, evict the one that was least recently accessed. Insert the new item with a frequency of one and update its timestamp. Return a list of the final items residing in the cache. A sequence of repeated and distinct requests should yield the correct retained items.

title: Text Sequence Differencer
spec: Develop a function `diff(documents)` that computes the longest common subsequence between two text versions provided as a tuple of two lists of words. Construct a two dimensional grid where the rows represent words from the first version and columns represent words from the second. Iterate through the grid, placing a diagonal increment when the words match, or the maximum of the top or left cells when they differ. Once the grid is fully populated, backtrack from the bottom right corner to reconstruct the sequence of edits. Determine whether each word was inserted, deleted, or kept unchanged. Return a sequence of tuples indicating the action and the word. Comparing two slightly modified sentences should return the step by step edit instructions.

title: Network Routing Simulator
spec: Write a simulator `route(packets)` that models data moving through a series of network nodes. Each packet is a tuple containing a destination address, a payload, and a time to live counter. Define a basic routing table that maps address prefixes to specific next hop nodes. For each packet, inspect its destination and find the longest matching prefix in the routing table to determine the next node. Decrement the time to live counter for every hop. If the counter reaches zero before the destination is found, discard the packet and generate an error message string. Accumulate all successfully delivered payloads in a list grouped by their final destination. Return a tuple containing the grouped deliveries and the list of dropped packets.

title: Genetic Population Evolver
spec: Implement a function `evolve(population)` that advances a group of digital organisms through a single generation. Each organism is represented by a binary sequence. First, calculate the fitness score for every sequence by summing its active bits and squaring the result. Select the top fifty percent of the population to act as parents for the next generation. Pair the parents sequentially and perform a crossover operation by swapping the second half of their binary sequences. Next, introduce random mutations by flipping exactly one bit in a small percentage of the new offspring. Combine the surviving parents and the new offspring to form the new generation. Return a tuple of the highest fitness score and the new population list.

title: Simple Raycaster Engine
spec: Create an engine `raycast(map)` that calculates the distance to walls for a first person perspective view. The input map is a two dimensional grid of zeros for empty space and ones for walls, passed alongside the player's coordinate and viewing angle. Cast sixty rays spreading across the field of view. For each ray, step forward in small increments along its angle and check the current grid cell. Stop the ray as soon as it intersects a cell containing a one. Calculate the Euclidean distance from the player to the intersection point and apply a cosine correction to prevent visual fish eye distortion. Return a list of the calculated distances for all sixty rays.

title: Dependent Knapsack Optimizer
spec: Design an optimizer `pack(items)` that solves a variation of the knapsack problem where some items require others to be selected first. Each item provides a weight, a value, and an optional prerequisite item identifier. Sort the items topologically based on their prerequisites to ensure dependencies are evaluated first. Construct a dynamic programming table tracking the maximum value for every weight limit up to fifty. When considering an item with a prerequisite, only update the table if the prerequisite item has already been included in the current weight configuration. Keep track of the selected items for the optimal combination. Return the maximum possible value and the sequence of chosen items.

title: Chord Progression Builder
spec: Write a function `compose(scale)` that generates a sequence of musical chords based on a given starting note and mode. Define a sequence of whole and half steps to represent major and minor scales. Generate the seven notes of the scale by applying the step pattern to the starting note. Build triads for each note by stacking the root, the third, and the fifth notes from the generated scale. Determine if each resulting chord is major, minor, or diminished based on the interval distances between its notes. Construct a standard progression using the first, fourth, fifth, and sixth chords of the scale. Return a list of tuples containing the chord name and its constituent notes.

title: Directory Synchronization Tool
spec: Develop a utility `sync(directories)` that compares a source file structure and a destination file structure to generate a list of update actions. The input is a tuple of two lists containing file paths, modification timestamps, and sizes. First, identify files present in the source but missing in the destination and mark them for copying. Next, find files present in both locations but with a newer timestamp or different size in the source, and mark them for updating. Finally, locate files that exist only in the destination and mark them for deletion to maintain an exact mirror. Return a list of action strings describing which files to copy, update, or delete.

title: Code Syntax Tokenizer
spec: Create a function `tokenize(code)` that scans a string of source code and breaks it into categorized syntax tokens. Iterate through the string character by character. When a letter is encountered, read until a non letter appears and check if the word is a reserved keyword or a standard variable name. When a quotation mark is found, read all characters until the closing quote and classify it as a string literal. Digits should be accumulated into numeric tokens, and mathematical symbols should be classified as operators. Discard any whitespace characters outside of string literals. Return a list of tuples where each contains the token type and the extracted string value.

title: Block Run Length Encoder
spec: Write a compressor `encode(image)` that processes a two dimensional grid of pixels using block based run length encoding. Instead of encoding row by row, divide the image into four by four pixel blocks. For each block, traverse the pixels in a zigzag pattern starting from the top left. Count consecutive pixels of the same color value. When the color changes, record the count and the color as a pair, then reset the counter for the new color. If an entire block consists of a single color, replace the block sequence with a special single byte compression code. Return the flattened sequence of encoded pairs and special codes.

title: Markdown Table Aligner
spec: Implement a formatter `align(rows)` that takes a list of unformatted text rows and converts them into a cleanly aligned markdown table. First, split each row by the pipe character and strip any leading or trailing spaces from the resulting cells. Determine the maximum width required for each column by examining the lengths of all cells in that vertical position. Create a separator row containing dashes that match the exact width of each column. Reconstruct every row by padding the cells with spaces so they perfectly align with the maximum widths. Insert the separator row immediately after the header row. Return the final table as a single formatted multiline string.

title: Simple Pattern Matcher
spec: Design a function `search(inputs)` that compares a text string against a custom pattern featuring wildcard characters. The input is a tuple containing the text string and the pattern string. The pattern supports a dot to match any single character and an asterisk to match zero or more of the preceding character. Use a recursive approach or a two dimensional dynamic programming grid to evaluate the match. When encountering an asterisk, branch the evaluation to cover cases where the preceding character appears multiple times or is completely skipped. For regular characters, ensure an exact match and advance the pointers for both the text and the pattern. Return a boolean true if the entire text string perfectly matches the pattern rules, or false otherwise.

title: Markup Tag Validator
spec: Create a function `validate(markup)` that parses a string of markup to ensure all opening tags are properly closed and nested. Scan the text to extract all tags enclosed in angle brackets. Ignore self closing tags that end with a slash before the closing bracket. When a standard opening tag is found, push its name onto a stack. When a closing tag is encountered, check if it matches the name of the tag currently at the top of the stack. If it matches, pop the tag from the stack; if it differs or the stack is empty, record a syntax error. Return true if the stack is completely empty at the end, meaning all tags were perfectly balanced.

title: Lisp Tree Evaluator
spec: Write an evaluator `evaluate(tree)` that executes a nested list structure representing an abstract syntax tree. The first element of every list dictates the operation, such as addition, multiplication, or variable definition. If the operation is a definition, store the variable name and its evaluated value in a local environment dictionary. If it is an arithmetic operation, recursively evaluate all remaining elements in the list and apply the math function to the results. Handle nested lists seamlessly by passing the updated environment downwards. If an undefined variable is referenced, halt execution and return an error string. Given a deeply nested tree of operations, return the final computed number.

title: Grid Path Finder
spec: Implement a function `navigate(grid)` that finds the shortest path from the top left corner to the bottom right corner of a maze grid using pathfinding logic. Maintain an open list of nodes to evaluate and a closed list of already visited nodes. Calculate a cost score for each step based on the distance traveled from the start and a heuristic distance to the goal. Always expand the node with the lowest total cost from the open list. Check the four adjacent directions for passable terrain, updating their cost scores if a cheaper path is found. Keep track of the parent node for each step to reconstruct the final route. Return the sequence of coordinates forming the shortest path.

title: ATM Transaction Processor
spec: Process a batch of bank account operations to determine the final balances. The input is a list of action strings like deposit or withdraw followed by their respective amounts. Keep a running total initialized to zero, adding funds for deposits and deducting for withdrawals. Withdrawals only succeed if the balance is sufficient and the amount stays under the daily limit of five hundred. For balance checks, do not alter the total, but apply a small fee of two if a withdrawal occurs when the balance is below one hundred. Return a list of the remaining balances recorded after every single action, so a deposit of one hundred and withdrawal of fifty outputs one hundred followed by fifty. The entry function is `process(transactions)`.

title: Fantasy RPG Combat Resolver
spec: Simulate a turn based battle between a hero and a series of monster encounters. The hero begins with one hundred health and zero gold, taking ten damage from goblins and twenty damage from orcs while losing five gold to the latter. Defeating any monster immediately awards ten gold. Using a potion restores thirty health up to a maximum of one hundred, while a poison event inflicts five damage on every subsequent turn unless a fairy is found to remove it. Return a tuple containing the final health, collected gold, and a boolean indicating if the hero survived. For example, encountering a goblin then finding a potion results in full health and ten gold. The entry function is `battle(events)`.

title: Text Adventure Parser
spec: Navigate a player through a grid based map using directional text commands. The player starts at origin zero zero and holds no keys, moving north or south to change the vertical coordinate and east or west to change the horizontal coordinate. Encountering a locked door stops movement in that direction unless a key was discovered in a previous turn. Collecting treasure adds fifty to the score but spawns a trap that skips the player next turn. Return a tuple of the final horizontal and vertical coordinates along with the total score. For example, moving north then east to a treasure results in coordinates one one and a score of fifty. The entry function is `explore(commands)`.

title: Public Transit Ticket Pricing
spec: Calculate fare prices for passengers based on their demographics and travel distance. The base ticket price is two dollars plus fifty cents for every mile traveled. Passengers aged sixty five and older receive a fifty percent discount, while students receive a flat one dollar reduction on their total cost. Traveling during morning peak hours incurs a one dollar surcharge, and weekend travel applies a blanket twenty percent off the final calculated ticket price. Return a list of all calculated final ticket prices. For example, a student traveling ten miles during peak hours pays exactly six dollars. The entry function is `fare(trips)`.

title: Sensor Data Smoother
spec: Clean and analyze a stream of numerical temperature measurements from an industrial sensor. First, replace any negative value or zero with the previous valid measurement in the sequence and cap any extreme temperature exceeding one hundred at exactly one hundred. Next, apply a moving average by replacing each number with the average of itself and its immediate neighbors, leaving the ends unchanged. Identify sequences where the temperature increases strictly three times in a row and flag any sudden drop of more than twenty degrees between consecutive readings. Return the smoothed list of temperatures and the count of sudden drops. For example, an input of fifty and ten returns the averaged values and a drop count of one. The entry function is `clean(readings)`.

title: Solar System Gravity Simulator
spec: Calculate the positions of planets using a simplified one dimensional gravity model over discrete time steps. For each step, calculate the gravitational attraction between each pair of bodies based on their inverse distance. Update the velocities of all bodies simultaneously based on these accumulated forces, then move the bodies to their new positions. If two bodies cross paths or occupy the exact same position, combine them into a single larger body with their total mass and conserved momentum. Return the final positions and masses of the remaining bodies. For example, two bodies moving towards each other will eventually merge and their final combined state is returned. The entry function is `simulate(bodies)`.

title: Retail Discount Applier
spec: Compute the final checkout price for a shopping cart containing item prices and string categories. Sum the prices of all items to establish a subtotal, permanently halving the price of any item belonging to the clearance category. If the cart contains more than five items in total, apply a ten percent volume discount to the entire subtotal. Add a standard sales tax of eight percent, strictly exempting any items in the grocery category from this specific tax, and apply a flat five dollar store coupon at the end. Return the final calculated amount due. For example, a clearance item originally priced at twenty and a standard item at ten will total twenty before taxes. The entry function is `checkout(items)`.

title: Hotel Booking Manager
spec: Process a series of guest reservations to calculate total lodging revenue. Standard rooms cost one hundred a night, while luxury suites cost two hundred. Add a weekend premium of fifty per night for any stay extending longer than five consecutive days and give a loyalty discount of ten percent to returning guests marked in the system. Calculate a mandatory cleaning fee of thirty per stay, but waive this fee entirely for guests booking suites. Sum the revenue from all valid requests while ignoring any requests that specify zero days. For example, a standard room for two nights without loyalty discounts generates two hundred and thirty in revenue. The entry function is `book(requests)`.

title: Stock Portfolio Rebalancer
spec: Adjust a financial portfolio to match target allocation percentages across different assets. Calculate the total monetary value of all current assets combined to determine the ideal monetary value for each asset based on the provided target percentages. Find the exact difference between the current and ideal values for every holding. Generate sell instructions for any asset exceeding its target by more than five percent to free up capital, then generate buy instructions for the remaining underweight assets using only the newly freed capital. Return a list of all executed adjustment amounts. For example, if cash is overrepresented, instructions will be generated to allocate it to underweight stocks. The entry function is `rebalance(portfolio)`.

title: Machine Code Emulator
spec: Execute a sequence of simplified assembly instructions that manipulate a memory array. Maintain a primary accumulator initialized to zero and a memory array of ten integer slots. For a load command, read the value from the specified memory slot into the accumulator, and for a store command, write the accumulator back into memory. Modify the accumulator by the given constant for add or subtract commands, and if a jump is encountered when the accumulator is positive, advance the instruction pointer by the offset. Halt execution immediately if a halt instruction is read and return the final accumulator value. For example, loading five, adding ten, and subtracting three results in a final value of twelve. The entry function is `execute(instructions)`.

title: Baseball Inning Simulator
spec: Track the progress of a half inning of baseball given a list of batter outcomes. Keep track of strikes and balls for the current batter, where three strikes make an out and four balls make a walk that advances the batter to first base. A hit moves any existing base runners forward by an amount equal to the base value, and runs accumulate whenever a base runner crosses home plate. Clear the bases entirely when a home run occurs and end the simulation immediately upon recording three outs. Return a tuple of total runs scored and batters faced. For example, a single followed by a home run results in two runs scored. The entry function is `play(outcomes)`.

title: Crop Rotation Planner
spec: Determine the next season assignments for a grid of farm fields based on previous planting history. To maintain soil health, replace heavy feeding crops like corn with nitrogen fixing legumes and assign root crops to fields that previously held legumes. If a field was left entirely fallow, it must be planted with a heavy feeder next. Ensure that no two directly adjacent fields are assigned the exact same crop type to prevent pest spread, defaulting conflicting fields back to fallow. Return a list of the newly assigned crops. For example, fields previously planted with corn and fallow will be assigned legumes and heavy feeders respectively. The entry function is `plan(fields)`.

title: Spacecraft Power Manager
spec: Distribute limited electrical power among spacecraft subsystems based on priority. The life support system must always receive its full requested amount unconditionally, while the communication array receives power only if the total available remains above a critical safety threshold of fifty. Scientific instruments share whatever power remains equally among themselves. If the total requests exceed the primary supply, drain the auxiliary battery reserve to cover the shortfall and trigger a system wide alert if the reserve drops below ten percent. Return a list of power amounts granted to each system and the remaining battery level. For example, if life support requests one hundred and supply is ninety, the battery is drained by ten units. The entry function is `allocate(telemetry)`.

title: Coffee Shop Barista Queue
spec: Sequence customer drink orders to minimize overall wait times at a cafe. An espresso requires one minute to prepare, a latte takes three minutes due to the milk steaming process, and a blended frappuccino requires a full five minutes of preparation. The single barista can only work on one drink at a time and must process them in the exact order they arrived. Track the current global time to calculate the total wait duration for each customer from their arrival until their drink is finished, adding a one minute cleaning delay after every third drink. Return a list of individual customer wait times. For example, an espresso followed by a latte results in wait times of one minute and four minutes respectively. The entry function is `brew(orders)`.

title: Board Game Scoring Tracker
spec: Tally the final victory points for players in an economic board game. Award five points for every territory tile a player controls and grant one extra point for every three leftover resources in their personal supply. Deduct a strict ten points if a player holds an unfulfilled objective card at the end of the game. Identify the player with the highest total score to determine the winner, breaking any ties by awarding the victory to the tied player holding the most remaining resources. Return the winning score and the absolute margin of victory over the second place player. For example, controlling three territories and holding four resources results in a base score of sixteen. The entry function is `score(players)`.

title: Toy Hash Function
spec: Generate a simplified integer checksum from a given input string for educational purposes. Convert each character in the string to its standard ascii numerical integer value and pad the sequence with zeros until its total length is exactly a multiple of eight. Process the numbers sequentially in distinct blocks of eight by multiplying the first four numbers by a prime constant of thirty one and reversing the original order of the last four numbers. Calculate the bitwise exclusive or of all eight numbers combined and keep a running total of these block results, applying a modulo of one thousand to prevent overflow. Return the final integer checksum. For example, a short string padded with zeros produces a consistent integer hash based on the transformations. The entry function is `hash(message)`.

title: Water Treatment Plant Controller
spec: Manage the valves and pumps of a water treatment facility using daily sensor readings. Maintain a holding tank volume initially set to zero, opening the intake valve to add twenty units if the main water level drops below fifty. Activate the alkaline pump for one cycle if the ph reading falls below six, or activate the acid pump if the ph rises above eight. If the internal pressure exceeds one hundred, trigger an emergency vent which instantly reduces the holding volume by ten units, and transfer clean water to the city supply if all metrics remain within normal operating ranges. Return a list of all daily actions taken. For example, a low water level triggers the intake valve and returns a single intake action. The entry function is `control(sensors)`.

title: Exam Grading Curve
spec: Adjust a batch of student test scores using a multi step curving algorithm. First, identify and remove any score of absolute zero, assuming the student was absent for the exam. Find the highest remaining score in the class and calculate its difference from a perfect one hundred, then add this difference as a flat curve to all other student scores. Cap any adjusted score that exceeds one hundred back down to the maximum of one hundred and convert the final numerical scores to letter grades where ninety is an A. Count the total number of students who failed by scoring below sixty and return the list of letter grades alongside the failure count. For example, scores of zero and eighty curve up to produce an A and one absent removal. The entry function is `curve(scores)`.

title: Printer Spooler Logic
spec: Organize a queue of document print requests detailing page counts, color modes, and user roles. Separate the incoming jobs into a high priority queue for teachers and a normal queue for students, ensuring all high priority jobs are processed completely first. If a print job is in color and exceeds fifty pages, split it into two separate jobs to prevent printer jams, and if a black and white job is under five pages, move it to the very front of its respective queue. Calculate the total pages printed and ink units consumed, assuming color takes three units per page and black takes one. Return the processed job sequence and ink totals. For example, a priority color job of sixty pages is split into two thirty page segments. The entry function is `spool(jobs)`.

title: Auto Mechanic Diagnostic
spec: Evaluate a checklist of boolean car symptoms to generate a repair estimate. If the car will not crank and the headlights are dim, append a battery replacement to the recommended repair list. If the engine cranks but fails to start, append a spark plug inspection, and if the vehicle stalls while driving at speed, flag the fuel pump for replacement. If multiple engine related issues are flagged simultaneously, add a full diagnostic fee to the final bill. Calculate the estimated cost assuming fifty for the battery, one hundred for brakes, and two hundred for the fuel pump. Return the list of repairs and total cost. For example, squealing brakes and a stall return recommendations for brake pads and a fuel pump totaling three hundred. The entry function is `diagnose(symptoms)`.

title: Beehive Simulation
spec: Model the daily growth and resource gathering of a simplified honey bee colony. Track the colony population and total honey stores over time, where sunny days add honey equal to available flowers and rainy days halt gathering while consuming ten units of honey. If the weather turns cold, the colony consumes twenty units of honey to generate warmth, and every five days the queen lays eggs to increase the population by exactly fifty bees. If honey stores drop below zero, a portion of the population starves and dies. Return a tuple containing the final population count and remaining honey levels. For example, three sunny days followed by a cold day results in accumulated honey minus the twenty unit cold penalty. The entry function is `simulate(days)`.

title: Disk Defragmenter Map
spec: Rearrange a numerical list of file blocks representing a hard drive to optimize storage space. Iterate through the disk array to find scattered parts of each unique file identifier and shift all parts of a given file so they sit contiguously in memory without gaps. Keep system files, explicitly identified by negative numbers, completely locked in their original array positions. Move all empty space, represented by zeros, to the end of the disk, except those trapped between locked system files. Calculate the total number of individual blocks that had to be physically moved. Return the optimized disk layout and the final move count. For example, scattered pieces of file one are grouped together at the front of the array. The entry function is `defragment(disk)`.

title: Pizza Delivery Router
spec: Sequence a list of delivery coordinates and preparation times for a single driver starting at origin zero zero. Calculate the Manhattan distance from the shop to each delivery location and group the orders into two distinct batches based on whether they fall within a ten block radius. Deliver the closer batch entirely before proceeding to the farther batch, sorting the orders within each batch by their prep times so the oldest pizzas are delivered first. Track the driver's total distance traveled by summing the distances between consecutive stops. Return the final route sequence and total distance traveled. For example, a closer order is delivered before a distant order even if the distant order was prepared earlier. The entry function is `route(orders)`.

title: Synthesizer Envelope Generator
spec: Generate an audio amplitude envelope array over time using attack, decay, sustain, and release parameters. Create an empty audio array to hold the amplitude values, ramping the volume linearly from zero up to one hundred during the attack phase over the specified number of steps. During the decay phase, decrease the volume gradually from one hundred down to the target sustain level, then hold the volume exactly steady at the sustain level for ten discrete steps. Finally, during the release phase, fade the volume from the sustain level back down to zero while ensuring no calculated values ever drop below zero. Return the complete sequence of volume levels. For example, a short attack followed by immediate release produces a triangular spike in the amplitude array. The entry function is `generate(parameters)`.

title: Assembly Line Quality Control
spec: Inspect manufactured items using simulated sensor data for weight and visual flaws. An item passes inspection only if its weight is strictly between ninety and one hundred and ten, and its visual flaw score is below five. Classify items as scrap if the weight is too low, overweight if the weight is too high, and send them to the rework station if the weight is acceptable but the flaw score is too high. Keep a running tally of passed, scrap, overweight, and rework items throughout the shift, awarding a speed bonus point every time five items pass consecutively. Return the four tallies and the accumulated speed bonus. For example, a weight of one hundred with a flaw score of two passes inspection and increments the pass tally. The entry function is `inspect(items)`.

title: Car Rental Pricing
spec: A function that calculates the total cost of a car rental. The input is a list containing the driver age, rental duration in days, car class index, insurance option index, and miles driven. First, determine the daily rate based on the car class index, where zero is thirty, one is fifty, and two is eighty. Next, apply a young driver surcharge of fifteen per day if the age is under twenty five. Then, add insurance costs: option one adds ten per day, option two adds twenty, and zero adds nothing. After that, calculate a mileage fee if the miles driven exceed one hundred times the duration, charging twenty cents per extra mile. Next, add a fixed thirty dollar cleaning fee if the miles driven exceed one thousand. Then, if a sixth parameter representing late return hours is greater than zero, add twenty dollars per late hour. Finally, apply a ten percent discount to the entire total if the rental duration is seven days or longer. Return the final total rounded to two decimals. Example input: [20, 5, 1, 2, 600]. Output: 465.0.

title: Healthcare Claim Adjudicator
spec: A function that processes a medical claim. The input is a list containing the billed amount, provider network status as a boolean, procedure category index, deductible remaining, and out of pocket maximum remaining. First, reduce the billed amount by a negotiated rate discount of twenty percent if the provider is in network. Next, subtract the remaining deductible from the allowed amount, capping the deduction at the allowed amount. Then, calculate coinsurance on the remaining balance: twenty percent if in network, fifty percent if out of network. After that, check if the procedure category is zero for preventive care, which overrides coinsurance to zero. Next, add a fifty dollar copay if the procedure category is two for a specialist visit. Then, ensure the patient responsibility does not exceed the out of pocket maximum remaining. Finally, calculate the plan payment by subtracting patient responsibility from the allowed amount. Return a tuple of patient responsibility and plan payment. Example input: [1000.0, true, 1, 300.0, 500.0]. Output: [400.0, 400.0].

title: Loyalty Points System
spec: A function that calculates loyalty points earned for a purchase. The input is a list containing purchase amount, member tier index, first purchase flag as boolean, item category index, and payment method index. First, award base points equal to the purchase amount rounded down to the nearest integer. Next, apply a tier multiplier: tier one gets no multiplier, tier two gets fifty percent more, and tier three gets double points. Then, add a flat bonus of five hundred points if it is the first purchase. After that, check the item category: category two earns double base points as a promotional bonus. Next, deduct fifty points if the payment method is three, representing a third party processor fee. Then, if the purchase amount is exactly one hundred dollars, award a special hundred point milestone bonus. Next, cap the maximum points earned in a single transaction at ten thousand points. Finally, ensure the final points cannot be negative, setting them to zero if so. Return the final integer points. Example input: [150.5, 2, false, 2, 1]. Output: 525.

title: Electricity Bill Calculator
spec: A function that computes a monthly electricity bill. The input is a list containing total kilowatt hours, peak hours used, renewable energy opt in flag, customer type index, and days in billing cycle. First, calculate the base energy charge at ten cents per kilowatt hour. Next, add a peak usage surcharge of five cents for every peak hour kilowatt used. Then, if the renewable energy flag is true, add a flat environmental fee of ten dollars and two cents per total kilowatt hour. After that, assess a fixed daily grid access fee: fifty cents per day for customer type zero, and one dollar per day for type one. Next, apply a low usage discount of five dollars if total kilowatt hours are under one hundred. Then, apply state taxes of five percent on the entire subtotal. Finally, check if the total bill is less than a minimum charge of fifteen dollars, and if so, increase it to fifteen dollars. Return the final bill rounded to two decimals. Example input: [250, 50, true, 0, 30]. Output: 65.62.

title: Freight Shipping Quoting
spec: A function that determines the freight shipping cost. The input is a list of weight in kilograms, volume in cubic meters, distance in kilometers, hazardous material flag, express delivery flag, and destination zone index. First, calculate base cost using weight, charging two dollars per kilogram. Next, calculate dimensional weight by multiplying volume by one hundred and fifty, and if this exceeds actual weight, use it to recalculate the base cost. Then, multiply the base cost by the distance divided by one hundred. After that, add a hazardous material surcharge of five hundred dollars if the flag is true. Next, add twenty percent to the subtotal if express delivery is requested. Then, apply a destination zone adjustment: zone zero gets ten percent off, zone two adds a fifty dollar remote delivery fee. Finally, cap the maximum charge at ten thousand dollars unless it contains hazardous materials, which has no cap. Return the integer floor of the final cost. Example input: [100, 2.0, 500, false, true, 2]. Output: 3650.

title: Smart Home Thermostat Logic
spec: A function that determines the target indoor temperature for a smart home. The input is a list containing current hour, occupancy flag, outside temperature, window open flag, vacation mode flag, and day of week index. First, set the default target temperature to seventy two degrees. Next, if the house is unoccupied, reduce the target by five degrees to save energy. Then, if vacation mode is active, set the target to sixty degrees regardless of occupancy. After that, check the window open flag; if true, turn off heating by setting the target to forty degrees. Next, adjust for the time of day: if the hour is between twenty two and six, reduce the target by three degrees for sleep mode. Then, if it is a weekend, identified by day index five or six, increase the morning target by two degrees between hours eight and ten. Finally, if the outside temperature is below freezing, increase the target by one degree to prevent frozen pipes. Return the final integer target temperature. Example input: [23, true, 25, false, false, 4]. Output: 69.

title: Drone Delivery Router
spec: A function that calculates the viability and estimated time for a drone delivery. The input is a list of delivery distance in kilometers, payload weight in kilograms, wind speed in kilometers per hour, rain severity index, and restricted airspace flag. First, check if the restricted airspace flag is true, returning zero time immediately if so. Next, establish a base flight time at two minutes per kilometer. Then, add a weight penalty of one minute for every kilogram of payload over two kilograms. After that, adjust for wind: if wind speed exceeds twenty, add five minutes to the flight time; if it exceeds forty, return zero as it is too dangerous. Next, apply a rain slowdown, adding twenty percent to the flight time if the rain index is one, and fifty percent if it is two. Then, check the drone battery limit, which allows a maximum flight time of forty five minutes; return zero if the calculated time exceeds this. Finally, add a flat three minutes for takeoff and landing procedures. Return the total integer minutes. Example input: [10, 3.5, 15, 0, false]. Output: 24.

title: Subscription Billing Engine
spec: A function that calculates a monthly subscription invoice. The input is a list containing the base plan price, days active in the month, total days in the month, account credit balance, region tax code, upgrade charge, and downgrade refund. First, prorate the base plan price by multiplying it by the days active and dividing by total days. Next, add any mid month upgrade charges to the prorated amount. Then, subtract any downgrade refunds. After that, apply a ten percent loyalty discount if the base plan price is over one hundred dollars. Next, deduct the available account credit from the subtotal, ensuring the subtotal does not drop below zero. Then, calculate taxes based on the region code: code one adds five percent, code two adds eight percent, and code zero adds nothing. Finally, add a late fee of fifteen dollars if the previous invoice was unpaid, represented by an eighth boolean parameter in the input list. Return the final invoice amount rounded to two decimals. Example input: [120.0, 15, 30, 10.0, 2, 20.0, 0.0, false]. Output: 73.44.

title: Online Multiplayer Matchmaking
spec: A function that computes a player matchmaking score. The input is a list of player skill rating, average ping in milliseconds, wait time in seconds, preferred role index, and toxicity report count. First, start with the base skill rating. Next, expand the acceptable skill range by subtracting ten points for every thirty seconds of wait time, simulating a broadening search. Then, apply a ping penalty: subtract fifty points if the ping is above one hundred, and one hundred points if above two hundred. After that, adjust for role demand: if the preferred role is zero for support, add a priority bonus of two hundred points. Next, penalize toxic behavior by reducing the score by five hundred points for every toxicity report. Then, check if the player is a new user by looking for a skill rating exactly at the starting value of one thousand, adding a small fifty point protection buffer. Finally, ensure the final matchmaking score never drops below zero. Return the integer score. Example input: [1500, 120, 90, 0, 1]. Output: 1120.

title: Fraud Detection Scoring
spec: A function that calculates a risk score for a financial transaction. The input is a list containing transaction amount, user account age in days, distance from home in miles, time of day hour, international merchant flag, and consecutive transactions count. First, add ten risk points if the transaction amount exceeds five hundred dollars, and thirty points if it exceeds two thousand. Next, add twenty points if the account age is less than thirty days. Then, assess geographic risk by adding fifteen points if the distance from home exceeds fifty miles, and fifty points if it is an international merchant. After that, check the time of day: transactions between midnight and five in the morning add twenty five points. Next, monitor velocity by adding ten points for every consecutive transaction beyond three. Then, apply a trusted user discount by subtracting twenty points if the account age is over five years. Finally, cap the maximum risk score at one hundred points and return it. Example input: [750, 15, 10, 2, false, 5]. Output: 75.

title: Aquarium Water Manager
spec: A function that computes an overall health score for an aquarium. The input is a list containing temperature in celsius, ph level, ammonia parts per million, nitrate parts per million, salinity specific gravity, and filter days since cleaned. First, start with a perfect score of one hundred. Next, deduct five points for every degree the temperature is outside the optimal range of twenty four to twenty six degrees. Then, deduct ten points if the ph level is below six point five or above seven point five. After that, apply a severe penalty of thirty points if ammonia is greater than zero point one, as it is highly toxic. Next, deduct one point for every unit of nitrate above twenty. Then, for saltwater tanks indicated by a salinity greater than one, deduct fifteen points if the salinity is outside one point zero two zero to one point zero two six. Finally, deduct ten points if the filter has not been cleaned in over thirty days. Return the final score, bounded to a minimum of zero. Example input: [28, 7.8, 0.05, 30, 1.023, 35]. Output: 60.

title: Farm Irrigation Scheduler
spec: A function that determines the irrigation duration in minutes for a crop field. The input is a list of soil moisture percentage, rain forecast in millimeters, crop water need index, current temperature in celsius, and local water restriction flag. First, set a base irrigation time of sixty minutes. Next, if the soil moisture is above forty percent, reduce the time by thirty minutes, or set it to zero if above sixty percent. Then, subtract two minutes for every millimeter of forecasted rain. After that, adjust for the crop type: index one requires twenty extra minutes, and index two requires forty extra minutes. Next, increase the time by fifteen minutes if the temperature exceeds thirty degrees celsius to compensate for evaporation. Then, if the water restriction flag is true, cut the total calculated time in half. Finally, ensure the irrigation time does not exceed a hard system limit of one hundred and twenty minutes. Return the integer duration. Example input: [35, 10, 1, 32, true]. Output: 37.

title: Inventory Space Binning
spec: A function that calculates a storage handling score for an inventory item. The input is a list containing weight in kilograms, length in centimeters, width, height, fragility flag, and hazardous class index. First, calculate the volume by multiplying length, width, and height. Next, assign a base score equal to the volume divided by one thousand. Then, add twenty points if the weight exceeds twenty kilograms, indicating a heavy lift requirement. After that, if the fragility flag is true, add fifty points for careful handling. Next, adjust for hazardous materials: class one adds thirty points, class two adds one hundred points, and class zero adds none. Then, check for awkward dimensions by adding fifteen points if any single dimension exceeds one hundred centimeters. Next, apply a bulk discount by reducing the score by ten percent if the volume exceeds fifty thousand. Finally, round the score up to the nearest integer. Example input: [25, 120, 50, 20, true, 1]. Output: 226.

title: Restaurant Table Turnover Estimator
spec: A function that estimates the dining duration in minutes for a restaurant table. The input is a list containing party size, course count, kids in party flag, alcohol ordered flag, VIP status flag, and current restaurant occupancy percentage. First, establish a base time of forty five minutes. Next, add ten minutes for every additional person in the party beyond two. Then, add twenty minutes for each course ordered beyond the first main course. After that, if there are kids in the party, add fifteen minutes to account for slower dining. Next, if alcohol is ordered, add twenty five minutes as guests tend to linger. Then, check the VIP status flag; if true, add thirty minutes because staff allow them more relaxed pacing. Finally, if the restaurant occupancy is over ninety percent, apply a rush pressure reduction by subtracting ten percent from the total time to encourage faster turnover. Return the integer floor of the estimated minutes. Example input: [4, 3, true, true, false, 95]. Output: 130.

title: Bank Loan Approval
spec: A function that evaluates a bank loan and returns an approval score. The input is a list of credit score, monthly income, monthly debt, loan amount requested, employment months, and prior bankruptcy flag. First, start with a base score equal to the credit score. Next, subtract two hundred points if the prior bankruptcy flag is true. Then, calculate the debt to income ratio by dividing monthly debt by monthly income; if this ratio exceeds forty percent, subtract one hundred points. After that, assess employment stability by adding fifty points if employment months exceed twenty four, but subtracting fifty if under six months. Next, check the loan amount: subtract ten points for every ten thousand dollars requested over fifty thousand. Then, if the applicant earns a high income over ten thousand a month, add an extra seventy five points. Finally, if the final score is above seven hundred, cap it at seven hundred, and if it is below zero, set it to zero. Return the integer score. Example input: [720, 5000, 1500, 60000, 36, false]. Output: 700.

title: Gym Membership Access
spec: A function that validates entry to a gym facility and calculates an access code. The input is a list containing membership tier index, current hour, outstanding balance, guest pass count, class reservation flag, and age. First, assign a base code of one for basic tier and two for premium tier. Next, check if the outstanding balance is over fifty dollars; if so, change the code to negative one to deny access. Then, enforce off peak hours: if a basic member tries to enter between hours seventeen and twenty, change the code to negative two. After that, if the member is bringing a guest, reduce the guest pass count by one; if the count was already zero, change the code to negative three. Next, if the class reservation flag is true, add ten to the positive access codes to route them to the studio. Then, if the age is under eighteen, change the code to negative four unless they are in the premium tier. Finally, if any denial code was triggered, ensure the lowest negative number takes precedence. Return the integer code. Example input: [0, 18, 10.0, 1, false, 25]. Output: -2.

title: Car Wash Pricing Logic
spec: A function that determines the final price for a car wash. The input is a list of wash package index, vehicle size index, wax coating flag, interior detail flag, member status flag, and mud severity index. First, set the base price based on the package: index zero is ten dollars, one is fifteen, and two is twenty five. Next, add a five dollar surcharge for medium vehicles at size index one, and ten dollars for large vehicles at size index two. Then, if the wax coating flag is true, add eight dollars. After that, if the interior detail flag is true, add a flat twenty dollars plus two dollars for every unit of the vehicle size index. Next, assess the mud severity: if the index is above three, add a ten dollar heavy cleaning fee. Then, if the member status flag is true, apply a twenty percent discount to the running total. Finally, add a fixed one dollar environmental fee that is not subject to discounts. Return the total rounded to two decimals. Example input: [2, 2, true, true, true, 4]. Output: 62.60.

title: Greenhouse Climate Control
spec: A function that determines the energy load of a greenhouse climate system. The input is a list containing internal humidity percentage, external temperature in celsius, internal temperature in celsius, soil moisture, sunlight intensity index, and carbon dioxide parts per million. First, start with a base load of ten units. Next, if the internal temperature is below eighteen degrees, add thirty units for heating; if above twenty eight, add forty units for cooling. Then, if the humidity exceeds eighty percent, add twenty units to power the dehumidifiers. After that, check the sunlight index: if it is zero, add twenty five units for grow lights. Next, if the carbon dioxide level is below four hundred, add fifteen units for the injection system. Then, if the external temperature is very low, below five degrees, apply a fifteen percent increase to the total load for poor insulation efficiency. Finally, if the soil moisture drops below thirty percent, add ten units for the water pumps. Return the final integer load. Example input: [85, 2, 16, 40, 0, 350]. Output: 115.

title: Ride Sharing Matcher
spec: A function that calculates a driver attraction score for a ride request. The input is a list of distance to passenger in miles, trip distance in miles, passenger rating out of five, surge multiplier, driver car category, and airport drop off flag. First, assign base points equal to the trip distance multiplied by two. Next, subtract three points for every mile the driver is away from the passenger. Then, multiply the current subtotal by the surge multiplier. After that, add twenty points if the passenger rating is above four point eight, but subtract fifty points if it is below four point zero. Next, if the airport drop off flag is true, add forty points due to higher likelihood of a return trip. Then, if the driver car category is two for a luxury vehicle, subtract thirty points if the trip distance is under five miles, as short trips are unprofitable. Finally, cap the maximum score at two hundred points and return the integer floor. Example input: [3, 10, 4.9, 1.5, 1, true]. Output: 76.

title: Airline Baggage Fee Calculator
spec: A function that computes the total baggage fee for a passenger. The input is a list containing ticket class index, frequent flyer status index, bag weight in kilograms, bag length in centimeters, bag width, and bag height. First, set the base checked bag fee to thirty dollars. Next, waive the base fee by setting it to zero if the ticket class is one or higher, or if the frequent flyer status is two or higher. Then, add an overweight surcharge of fifty dollars if the bag weight exceeds twenty three kilograms, and one hundred dollars if it exceeds thirty two kilograms. After that, calculate the linear dimensions by summing length, width, and height; if this sum exceeds one hundred and fifty eight centimeters, add an oversize fee of seventy five dollars. Next, apply a ten percent discount to the total fees if the frequent flyer status is exactly one. Then, if the weight exceeds forty five kilograms, set the total fee to nine hundred and ninety nine dollars to indicate a hard rejection. Return the final integer fee. Example input: [0, 0, 25, 80, 50, 30]. Output: 155.

title: Escape Room Controller
spec: A function that calculates the final score for an escape room team. The input is a list of completion time in minutes, hints used, puzzles skipped, lock picking penalties, broken props count, and hidden coins found. First, start with a maximum score of ten thousand points. Next, subtract one hundred points for every minute taken over the par time of forty five minutes. Then, deduct five hundred points for each hint used. After that, apply a severe penalty of two thousand points for every puzzle skipped. Next, deduct three hundred points for each lock picking penalty triggered by forcing a mechanism. Then, for every broken prop, subtract one thousand points and immediately disqualify the team if the count exceeds two by returning a score of zero. Finally, add two hundred bonus points for each hidden coin found, but ensure the final score does not exceed the original ten thousand point maximum. Return the integer score. Example input: [50, 2, 0, 1, 0, 3]. Output: 8800.

title: Space Colony Life Support
spec: A function that determines the life support system power allocation in kilowatts. The input is a list of current crew count, oxygen level percentage, carbon dioxide level percentage, internal temperature, external radiation level, and solar panel output. First, allocate a base power of ten kilowatts per crew member. Next, if the oxygen level is below twenty percent, add fifty kilowatts to ramp up the oxygen generators. Then, if carbon dioxide exceeds one percent, add thirty kilowatts for the scrubbers. After that, adjust for temperature: if it is below eighteen degrees, add twenty kilowatts for heaters, and if above twenty six, add twenty five kilowatts for coolers. Next, if the external radiation level is above level five, add forty kilowatts to power the electromagnetic shields.
