Then, check the total allocated power against the solar panel output; if it exceeds the output, switch to emergency mode by halving the power to the heaters and coolers. Finally, round the final power allocation up to the nearest integer. Example input: [4, 19, 0.5, 17, 6, 120]. Output: 140.

title: Theme Park Fast Pass
spec: A function that calculates the cost of a theme park fast pass in credits. The input is a list containing ride popularity index, time slot hour, current crowd level percentage, guest VIP tier, consecutive passes bought, and group size. First, assign a base cost of fifty credits. Next, add twenty credits if the ride popularity index is one, and fifty credits if it is two. Then, apply a peak hour surcharge of thirty credits if the time slot is between thirteen and sixteen. After that, if the crowd level exceeds eighty percent, multiply the current subtotal by one point five. Next, subtract a discount of twenty credits if the guest is in VIP tier one, or forty credits if tier two. Then, penalize hoarding by adding ten credits for every consecutive pass bought beyond three. Finally, apply a group discount: if the group size is five or more, reduce the final total by ten percent. Return the integer floor of the final cost. Example input: [2, 14, 85, 1, 4, 6]. Output: 166.

title: Pet Boarding Scheduler
spec: A function that calculates the daily boarding rate for a pet. The input is a list of dog weight in pounds, aggression history flag, required walk count, medication doses per day, intact male flag, and stay duration in days. First, establish a base rate of forty dollars. Next, add ten dollars if the weight exceeds fifty pounds, and twenty dollars if it exceeds one hundred pounds. Then, if the aggression history flag is true, add a twenty five dollar hazard fee. After that, add five dollars for every requested walk beyond the standard two walks. Next, add three dollars for each medication dose required per day. Then, if the intact male flag is true, add a fifteen dollar isolation surcharge. Finally, apply a long stay discount by subtracting ten percent from the total daily rate if the stay duration is fourteen days or longer. Return the final rate rounded to two decimals. Example input: [60, false, 4, 2, true, 15]. Output: 72.90.

title: Mining Truck Dispatcher
spec: A function that evaluates a mining truck's priority score for the crusher queue. The input is a list of ore grade percentage, current wait time in minutes, fuel remaining percentage, tire wear index, payload weight in tons, and shift end proximity in minutes. First, start with a base score equal to the payload weight. Next, add two points for every percentage of ore grade above fifty percent to prioritize high quality material. Then, add one point for every minute the truck has been waiting. After that, if the fuel remaining is below fifteen percent, add fifty emergency points so the truck can dump and refuel. Next, penalize poor maintenance by subtracting twenty points if the tire wear index is three or higher. Then, if the shift ends in less than thirty minutes, add forty points to clear the truck before driver changeover. Finally, cap the maximum priority score at three hundred points to prevent system overflow. Return the integer score. Example input: [65, 20, 10, 2, 150, 15]. Output: 290.

title: Global Call Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(availabilities)` that finds the earliest one hour slot where all participants are available. Each participant provides a list of their available intervals as tuples of start and end hours. The slot must fall on a weekday based on a given day offset. If no overlap exists, try removing the participant with the fewest available hours and check again. Additionally, any slot before eight morning or after eight evening local time requires a penalty score. If the best slot has a penalty, attempt to shift it forward by one hour to see if the penalty clears. Return the chosen start hour, the number of attendees, and the final penalty score, or a failure tuple if less than three can attend.

title: Character Build Validator
spec: Create a function `validate(attributes)` that checks if a new role playing game character meets all creation rules. The input is a list of integers representing strength, dexterity, constitution, intelligence, wisdom, and charisma. First calculate the total points to ensure they do not exceed seventy five. Then verify that no single attribute is higher than eighteen or lower than eight. Next, check class requirements by ensuring at least one attribute is exactly eighteen and another is above fourteen. Apply a racial bonus by adding two to the lowest score, adjusting for any ties by picking the first one. Also, check if wisdom is greater than intelligence, which grants a magic resistance flag. If charisma is exactly eight, reduce the maximum allowed points by five and recheck the total. Return a boolean indicating if the build is legal, the adjusted attributes, and the magic flag.

title: Meal Planner Filter
spec: Implement a function `filter(meals)` that takes a list of lists of ingredient strings and removes meals violating common dietary rules. First, discard any meal containing meat if the meal also contains dairy. Second, flag meals with nuts and ensure they have a warning string added to their list. Third, if a meal has more than five ingredients, remove the last ingredient to simplify it. Fourth, reject any meal that lacks at least one vegetable from a known list of standard greens like spinach or kale. Fifth, count the number of spicy ingredients and remove the meal if it contains more than two. Finally, sort the remaining meals by their ingredient count in descending order. Return a tuple containing the number of rejected meals and the finalized list of accepted meals.

title: Secure Token Generator
spec: Develop a function `generate(seed)` that produces a list of integers representing a security token based on a starting number. Multiply the starting number by an odd prime and take the remainder modulo one thousand. Extract the digits of this result and reverse their order. For each digit, if it is even, add seven; if it is odd, subtract three. If a modified digit falls below zero, convert it to its absolute value. Then compute the running sum of all modified digits and append this sum to the sequence. Next, identify any duplicate adjacent numbers in the sequence and remove the second occurrence. Finally, swap the first and last elements of the sequence before returning it.

title: Conveyor Belt Sorter
spec: Write a function `sort(packages)` to route items on a factory line. The input is a list of tuples containing item weight, volume, and a material integer code. Packages weighing over fifty units go to the heavy chute, returning a one. Packages with a volume above one hundred go to the bulky chute, returning a two. If the material code is exactly seven, the item is fragile and overrides weight rules to go to chute three. If the material code is nine, the item requires inspection and must go to chute five regardless of other properties. Standard items not meeting these criteria go to chute four. Accumulate the total count for each chute. Calculate the total weight of items routed to chute one. Return the counts as a five element tuple and the total heavy weight.

title: Signal Noise Reducer
spec: Implement a function `clean(frequencies)` that processes a list of decimal numbers representing audio frequencies. First, remove any frequency below twenty or above twenty thousand as they are outside human hearing. Next, identify any sudden spikes where a value is more than double the previous value and reduce it by half. Then apply a moving average smoothing using a window of three elements. After smoothing, if any value is exactly zero, replace it with a one to avoid silence errors. Count how many resulting values fall into the vocal range between eighty and two hundred and fifty five. Find the maximum frequency in the final cleaned list. Return the smoothed list, the vocal count, and the maximum value.

title: Vegetable Patch Organizer
spec: Create a function `plant(dimensions)` that calculates the maximum number of crops fitting in a grid. The input is a tuple of width and length. Allocate the first two rows entirely for tomatoes which require three units of space each. Assign the perimeter of the remaining area to marigolds to deter pests, spacing them one unit apart. Fill the interior space alternating between carrots and beans, where beans need twice the space of carrots. Leave the exact center coordinate empty to serve as a walking path. If the total space is insufficient for at least one of each plant, return a list of zeros. Tally the total count of each plant type based on these spatial rules. Return a list of four integers representing the counts.

title: Subscriber Retention Scorer
spec: Develop a function `score(history)` to evaluate if a user might cancel their service. The input is a list of integers denoting the number of logins per month for the past year. Calculate the average logins for the first six months and compare it to the last six months. If the recent average has dropped by more than thirty percent, add fifty risk points. Next, check if there are three consecutive months with zero logins, which adds another thirty points. If the user had a perfect login record of daily logins in any single month, subtract fifteen points. If the very last month shows an increase over the previous month, subtract twenty points. Cap the final score at one hundred and ensure it does not drop below zero. Return the final risk score and a boolean indicating if the score exceeds seventy.

title: Star Catalog Matcher
spec: Write a function `identify(observations)` that cross references a list of observed celestial coordinates with known rules. Each observation is a tuple of right ascension, declination, and brightness magnitude. If the brightness is less than zero, classify it as a planet and increment the planet count. If the declination is above eighty, classify it as a polar star regardless of brightness. For all other items, if the right ascension falls between ten and fourteen, mark them as deep sky objects. If the declination is negative and the brightness is between two and five, classify it as a southern hemisphere target. Ignore any observations that have a right ascension of exactly zero due to sensor noise. Accumulate all these classifications. Return a list containing the counts for each of the four categories.

title: Hexagonal Grid Navigator
spec: Implement a function `navigate(directions)` that calculates the final coordinates of a robot on a hex grid. The input is a list of integers from zero to five representing movement directions. Start the robot at origin coordinates zero zero zero. For each step, adjust the three cubic coordinates according to standard flat topped hex grid movements. If a step moves the robot further than ten units from the origin, ignore that step as an out of bounds error and increment an error counter. If the robot returns to the exact origin during the path, add a loop flag to a log. After processing all steps, calculate the distance from the origin by finding the maximum absolute value among the three coordinates. Return the final three coordinates as a tuple, the computed distance, and the error count.

title: Property Value Estimator
spec: Create a function `estimate(features)` that calculates the price of a house. The input is a list of integers representing square footage, number of bedrooms, age in years, and condition rating from one to five. Base price starts at the square footage multiplied by one hundred and fifty. Add ten thousand for each bedroom up to a maximum of four. Subtract five hundred for every year of age, but cap the depreciation at fifty thousand. If the property is older than fifty years, add a historical bonus of twenty thousand. Multiply the total by a condition modifier where a rating of three is neutral, five adds twenty percent, and one subtracts twenty percent. If the final price exceeds five hundred thousand, apply a luxury tax reduction of five percent. Return the final adjusted integer price.

title: Telemetry Packet Decoder
spec: Develop a function `decode(stream)` that parses a sequence of integer bytes from a sensor network. The first byte indicates the payload length, so extract exactly that many subsequent bytes. The next byte is the sensor type where one means temperature and two means pressure. If it is temperature, convert the remaining bytes into an integer and subtract fifty to handle negative values. If it is pressure, sum the bytes and multiply by ten. If the sensor type is three, treat the bytes as a sequence of boolean status flags. Count any remaining unparsed bytes in the stream as trailing garbage. If the garbage count is greater than five, append a warning flag. Return a tuple of the decoded value, the sensor type, and the garbage count.

title: Meal Macros Calculator
spec: Write a function `tally(ingredients)` that computes total calories and macronutrients. The input is a list of tuples containing protein, carbohydrate, and fat amounts in grams. Multiply protein and carbohydrates by four to get their calories, and multiply fat by nine. Sum these to find the total caloric value for each ingredient. If an ingredient has more fat than carbohydrates, classify it as keto friendly and increment a counter. If an ingredient has more than twenty grams of protein, mark it as high protein. Aggregate the total grams of each macronutrient across all ingredients. Deduct a small fiber baseline of two grams from the total carbohydrates if the total exceeds fifty. Return a tuple containing the total calories, the keto friendly count, the high protein count, and the three macronutrient totals.

title: Poetry Contest Judges
spec: Implement a function `evaluate(lines)` that scores a submitted poem provided as a list of strings. First, count the number of lines and award five points if it is exactly fourteen, acting as a sonnet bonus. Next, check the last word of each line and add ten points for every consecutive pair of lines that end with the same letter. Calculate the average word count per line and deduct points if it is less than five or greater than twelve. Check for the presence of specific seasonal words like winter or spring and add a point for each. If any line contains a banned offensive word, immediately set the score to zero and halt further evaluation. Return the final integer score.

title: Worker Shift Assigner
spec: Create a function `assign(requests)` that matches workers to daily shifts. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list contains the preferred shift integers for a worker. The factory needs exactly three workers per shift across three shifts. Iterate through the workers and place them in their first available preference. If a shift becomes full, assign the remaining workers to their second or third choices. Ensure that no worker is assigned to two consecutive shifts. If a worker cannot be placed in any preferred shift, assign them to a reserve pool. Additionally, designate the first assigned worker in each shift as the shift lead. Return a list of lists showing the assigned worker indices for each shift, followed by the reserve pool list.

title: Material Storage Router
spec: Develop a function `route(shipments)` that decides where incoming goods should be stored. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer volume and a boolean hazardous flag. The main facility has a capacity of one thousand units, while the secondary facility holds five hundred. Iterate through the shipments and add them to the main facility until it is full. Once the main facility overflows, route the exact remainder of that shipment to the secondary facility. If a shipment contains hazardous materials indicated by the flag, it must skip the main facility entirely and go to the secondary. Any subsequent shipments go entirely to the secondary facility until it too is full. Count how many shipments are completely rejected due to lack of space in both facilities. Return the utilized capacity of both facilities and the rejected count.

title: Ledger Discrepancy Finder
spec: Write a function `reconcile(records)` that compares internal bank logs with external clearing house logs. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer id, an amount, and a type string. Separate the records into internal and external lists based on the type string. Match them by id to ensure the amounts are identical. If an id is missing from the external list, append it to a pending list. If an id is missing from the internal list, mark it as unauthorized. If the amounts differ, calculate the absolute difference and add it to an error sum. Flag any individual difference greater than one thousand as a critical audit failure. Return the total error sum, the length of the pending list, the count of unauthorized transactions, and the critical failure boolean.

title: Forest Fire Spread
spec: Implement a function `simulate(grid)` that calculates one time step of a wildfire. The input is a list of lists of integers where zero is empty, one is a tree, and two is burning. Create a new grid of the same dimensions to store the next state. A burning cell turns into an empty cell. A tree cell becomes a burning cell if at least one orthogonally adjacent neighbor is burning. Furthermore, an empty cell has a small chance of spontaneously growing a tree if surrounded by at least three trees, represented by a deterministic modulo check on its coordinates. If a burning cell is adjacent to a water cell, represented by a three, the fire is extinguished and it becomes an empty cell immediately. Return the updated grid and the count of newly burned trees.

title: Airline Seating Group
spec: Create a function `group(passengers)` that assigns boarding zones. The input is a list of tuples containing an integer row number, a seat letter string, and a frequent flyer boolean. First, assign zone one to anyone with the frequent flyer flag. Next, assign zone two to passengers in rows one through ten. Then assign zone three to window seats, which are letters a and f, provided they are in rows eleven through twenty. If a passenger is traveling with an infant flag, upgrade them to zone two regardless of row. All remaining passengers fall into zone four. Count the number of passengers in each of the four zones. Find the highest row number occupied by any passenger. Return a list of these four counts and the maximum row number.

title: Waveform Phase Shifter
spec: Develop a function `modulate(signal)` that alters a sequence of integer amplitudes. Iterate through the list and invert the sign of every third element. If an amplitude exceeds fifty, clamp it to exactly fifty. If an amplitude is below negative fifty, clamp it to negative fifty. If the sequence contains two consecutive zero values, insert a value of ten between them to keep the transmitter active. Compute the absolute sum of all altered values to represent the transmission energy. Finally, discard any trailing values that are exactly zero to shorten the transmission. Return the modified list, the calculated energy integer, and the length of the final sequence.

title: Shopping Cart Promotions
spec: Write a function `calculate(cart)` that applies various promotions to a shopping basket. The input is a list of integer prices. First, sum the prices to get a subtotal. If the subtotal is over one hundred, apply a ten percent reduction. Next, find the most expensive individual item and subtract five from its price as a special coupon, ensuring its price does not drop below zero. If the cart contains more than five items, waive the standard shipping fee of ten; otherwise add it to the total. Apply a strict sales tax of five percent to the final amount. Count how many items cost exactly ninety nine before discounts. Return the final total cost and the count of ninety nine priced items.

title: Weather Trend Analyzer
spec: Implement a function `analyze(temperatures)` that finds patterns in daily readings. The input is a list of integers. Find the longest consecutive streak of days where the temperature increased. Calculate the median temperature by sorting the list and picking the middle element. Count how many days the temperature dropped below freezing, which is thirty two degrees. If the freezing count is greater than ten, append a frost warning integer flag of one to the results. Find the largest single day temperature drop. If the maximum temperature exceeds one hundred, add a heatwave warning flag of two. Return a tuple containing the longest streak, the median value, the freezing count, the drop magnitude, and the two warning flags.

title: Text Digit Corrector
spec: Create a function `correct(characters)` that cleans up scanned numerical data. The input is a list of single character strings. Replace any letter o with the digit zero, and any lowercase l with the digit one. If a decimal point appears more than once, remove all subsequent occurrences. Check if the sequence ends with a dash and remove it, as it signifies a scanning artifact. If the string contains any remaining alphabetic characters, remove them entirely to isolate the numbers. Finally, join the characters into a single string and attempt to parse it into a decimal number, returning a default of zero if it fails. Return the corrected string, the parsed number, and the count of removed alphabetic characters.

title: Reservoir Flow Regulator
spec: Develop a function `regulate(levels)` that controls water flow based on reservoir data. The input is a list of integers representing water depth in meters. If the depth exceeds eighty, activate the primary release valve by setting the first output flag to true. If the depth is below twenty, engage the emergency refill pump by setting the second flag to true. Additionally, if the depth drops by more than ten meters between any two consecutive readings, trigger an alarm flag. Count how many readings are exactly optimal at fifty meters. If the final reading is below the initial reading, set a negative trend flag. Calculate the average depth over the entire list. Return a tuple of the flags, the optimal count, and the average depth.

title: Checksum Digit Validator
spec: Write a function `verify(sequence)` that checks a custom identification number. The input is a list of exactly ten integers. Multiply the first, third, and fifth digits by three. Multiply the second, fourth, and sixth digits by seven. Sum all these modified digits along with the unmodified seventh, eighth, and ninth digits. If the sum is zero, automatically mark the sequence as invalid. Calculate the remainder when this sum is divided by ten. If this remainder matches the tenth digit, the sequence is valid. Furthermore, check that no digit repeats more than three times consecutively, failing the sequence if so. Return a boolean for validity, the calculated remainder, and the sum.

title: Music Playlist Generator
spec: Write a function `shuffle(tracks)` where tracks is a list of tuples containing title, artist, tempo, and genre. Calculate total playtime assuming each track is three minutes. Group the tracks by artist. Select tracks ensuring no artist is played twice in a row. Drop any tracks with a tempo below sixty. Alternate between fast and slow tempos, considering a tempo over one hundred twenty as fast. Ensure the first track is fast and the last track is slow. If a genre repeats three times in sequence, insert a random different genre if available. Return a list of titles. Example: given track A by artist X at 130 tempo rock, track B by artist Y at 80 tempo pop, returns track A then track B.

title: Email Thread Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(emails)` where emails is a list of strings representing lines of an email thread. Look for lines starting with From or To and extract the email addresses. If a line contains a forward slash and the word wrote, treat the rest of the message as a quoted reply and strip it from the final output. Remove lines that only contain dashes or stars used as separators. Detect automatic signatures starting with Best or Regards and remove them along with everything after them. Concatenate the remaining lines into a single message string. Return a tuple containing a list of unique email addresses found and the clean message string. Example: given From alice at test, Hello, Regards, Alice, returns a list with alice at test and the string Hello.

title: Pluralization Engine
spec: Write a function `pluralize(words)` where words is a list of noun strings. Apply rules to pluralize each word. If it ends in s, x, z, ch, or sh, add es. If it ends in a consonant followed by y, change y to ies. If it ends in f or fe, change to ves, but for words ending in ff just add s. If it ends in a vowel followed by o, add s. If it ends in a consonant followed by o, add es. Handle irregulars like child to children, person to people, mouse to mice, foot to feet, and tooth to teeth. Handle unchanged words like sheep, deer, and fish. Otherwise, just add s. Return the list of pluralized words. Example: given cat and sheep, returns cats and sheep.

title: Cinema Seating Allocator
spec: Write a function `seat(groups)` where groups is a list of integer group sizes. Maintain a list of twenty empty seats represented by zeros. For each group, search for a contiguous block of zeros equal to the group size, starting from the left side of the row. If a block is found, fill it with the group size integer. Ensure there is at least one empty seat left between different groups as a buffer. If a group cannot fit, skip it and try the next group, tracking how many groups were rejected. Return a tuple of the final row list and the rejected count. Example: given sizes three, five, and fifteen, returns a row with three threes, a zero, five fives, and eleven zeros, with one rejection.

title: Chat Message Formatter
spec: Write a function `format(messages)` where messages is a list of tuples containing sender name, timestamp, and text. Sort the messages by timestamp in ascending order. If the text is empty, drop the message entirely. If the sender is the word system, wrap the text in square brackets. If the text contains the word badword, replace it with asterisks. If consecutive messages are from the same sender within five minutes, group them into a single block under one sender header. Capitalize the first letter of each sentence in the text. Add a blank line between different sender blocks. Return a single formatted string of the chat history. Example: given user A saying hi at one and user A saying there at two, returns a single block for user A with Hi and There.

title: Hospital Triage Priority
spec: Write a function `triage(patients)` where patients is a list of tuples containing name, age, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, and pain level. Assign a base score of zero to each patient. Add three points if heart rate is over one hundred twenty or under fifty. Add three points if respiratory rate is over thirty. Add two points if temperature is over thirty nine or under thirty five. Add one point if pain level is eight or higher. If age is over sixty five or under five and they have any other points, add an extra two points. Sort the patients by score in descending order, then by their original arrival index. Return a list of patient names in order. Example: given normal Bob and high pain Alice, returns Alice then Bob.

title: Video Game Achievement Tracker
spec: Write a function `unlock(actions)` where actions is a list of tuples containing an action name and a value. Track totals for enemies defeated, coins collected, and levels completed. Award achievement one if enemies defeated reaches one hundred. Award achievement two if coins collected reaches five hundred. Award achievement three if a single level completed action has a value under three hundred, simulating a speedrun. Award achievement four if all three categories have at least one logged action. Ensure each achievement is only awarded once. Return a list of awarded achievement names in the order they were unlocked. Example: given coins collected five hundred, returns a list containing achievement two.

title: Frequent Flyer Tier Adjuster
spec: Write a function `tier(flyers)` where flyers is a list of tuples containing flyer name, miles, and days since last flight. Bronze is under one thousand miles, Silver is one to five thousand, and Gold is above five thousand. If days since last flight is over three hundred, deduct five hundred miles for inactivity. If miles drop below zero, reset them to zero. If a flyer took a flight within thirty days, give a bonus of one hundred miles. Recalculate tiers based on these adjusted miles. If a flyer drops a tier, add a warning flag string to their profile. If a flyer reaches Gold, add a VIP flag string. Return a list of tuples containing the name, new miles, new tier, and flag status. Example: given John with five thousand miles and ten days, returns John, five thousand one hundred, Gold, VIP.

title: Automated Text Summarizer
spec: Write a function `summarize(sentences)` where sentences is a list of string sentences. Exclude sentences with fewer than five words. Calculate term frequency across all valid sentences, ignoring capitalization. Exclude common stop words like the, a, an, and, or, and but. Score each sentence by summing the frequencies of its words, then divide the score by its word count to get an average. Give a twenty percent bonus score to the very first sentence. Give a ten percent bonus score to any sentence containing an exclamation mark. Select the top three sentences by their final score and return them in their original order. Example: given four sentences, returns the three highest scoring ones chronologically.

title: Digital Logic Circuit Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(gates)` where gates is a list of tuples containing gate type, input one index, and input two index. Maintain a state array of signals initially set to zero. Evaluate each gate sequentially. For an AND gate, the output is one if both inputs are one. For an OR gate, the output is one if either input is one. For an XOR gate, the output is one if inputs differ. For a NOT gate, ignore the second input and output the inverse of the first input. If an input index is negative, treat it as a hardcoded one. If an input index is out of bounds, treat it as a zero. Append each gate result to the state array. Return the final output signal of the last gate. Example: given AND with two negative ones, returns one.

title: Audio Equalizer Band Adjuster
spec: Write a function `equalize(bands)` where bands is a list of integer frequencies representing an audio spectrum. Identify bass frequencies as below sixty, mid as between sixty and three hundred, and treble as above three hundred. Boost bass frequencies by adding ten, capped at a maximum of one hundred. Reduce mid frequencies by five, floored at zero. Leave treble unchanged unless it exceeds ninety, in which case reduce it to ninety. Apply a smoothing pass where each band becomes the integer average of itself and its immediate neighbors. The first and last bands only average with their single neighbor. Return the adjusted list of frequencies. Example: given fifty, returns fifty five after boost and smoothing.

title: Data Deduplication String Matcher
spec: Write a function `deduplicate(records)` where records is a list of string names. Convert all names to lowercase and strip leading and trailing whitespace. Remove any special characters, keeping only letters and spaces. Replace multiple consecutive spaces with a single space to create a canonical name. For each new name, compare it against existing canonical names in a unique list. If the length difference is greater than three, they do not match. Count matching characters at the same positions up to the length of the shorter string. If matching characters exceed eighty percent of the longer string, consider it a duplicate and discard it. Otherwise, add it to the unique list. Return the unique list. Example: given John Doe and john doe, returns one John Doe.

title: Train Network Timetable Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(arrivals)` where arrivals is a list of tuples containing station id, arrival time in minutes, and departure time in minutes. Ensure a train does not depart before it arrives. Verify the dwell time, which is departure minus arrival, is at least two minutes but does not exceed fifteen minutes. Check that the travel time to the next station, meaning next arrival minus current departure, is at least five minutes. Ensure successive station ids are not identical. Verify the train visits at least three stations. Return a list of error strings detailing any violations, or an empty list if the timetable is fully valid. Example: given two stations only, returns an error stating minimum stations not met.

title: Dietary Constraint Checker
spec: Write a function `audit(meals)` where meals is a list of tuples containing meal name and a list of ingredients. Define known allergens as peanuts, shellfish, dairy, and soy. Define meat ingredients as beef, chicken, pork, and fish. A meal is considered vegan if it contains no meat and no dairy. A meal is considered safe if it contains no allergens. If any ingredient contains the word artificial, flag the meal as processed. Skip any meal that has zero ingredients. Collect warnings for each meal as a tuple of meal name, a boolean for vegan, a boolean for safe, and a boolean for processed. Return a list of the collected tuples. Example: given salad with peanuts, returns salad, true, false, false.

title: Insurance Premium Calculator
spec: Write a function `quote(profiles)` where profiles is a list of tuples containing age, vehicle age, accidents, and daily mileage. Start with a base premium of five hundred. Add two hundred if the age is under twenty five, or add one hundred if the age is over sixty five. Add fifty for comprehensive risk if the vehicle age is less than three years. Add one hundred and fifty for each accident. If accidents exceed three, deny coverage by returning zero for that specific profile. Add seventy five if daily mileage exceeds fifty. Finally, apply a ten percent discount if the total premium before the discount is over one thousand. Return a list of integer premiums. Example: given a twenty year old with no accidents, returns seven hundred.

title: Automated Negotiation Agent
spec: Write a function `negotiate(offers)` where offers is a list of integer price offers from a buyer. The seller starts with a target asking price of one thousand and a minimum acceptable price of eight hundred. For the first offer, if it is above eight hundred, accept immediately and return it. For subsequent offers, reduce the seller asking price by fifty. If the asking price drops below the minimum, lock it at the minimum. If the buyer offer is within fifty of the current asking price, compromise and return the midpoint integer. If the buyer offer is under five hundred, reject it completely and return zero to end negotiations. Return the final agreed price, or zero if no agreement is reached. Example: given nine hundred as first offer, returns nine hundred.

title: Peer-to-peer File Piece Selector
spec: Write a function `select(pieces)` where pieces is a list of tuples containing piece index, rarity score, size, and a downloaded boolean. Filter out any pieces that are already downloaded. If no pieces remain, return negative one. Identify the piece with the lowest rarity score to implement a rarest first strategy. If multiple pieces tie for the lowest score, prefer the one with the smaller size. If still tied, pick the one with the lowest piece index. If the rarity score of the chosen piece is above fifty, it is too common, so switch strategy and instead return the piece with the absolute smallest size to finish quickly. Return the integer index of the selected piece. Example: given an undownloaded piece with rarity ten, returns its index.

title: Virtual Memory Page Replacement
spec: Write a function `page(requests)` where requests is a list of page accesses as tuples containing page id and a write boolean. Memory can hold exactly four pages. Maintain a list of pages currently in memory, their last access times, and their dirty bits. For each access, increment a global time counter. If the page is in memory, update its access time, and set its dirty bit to true if it is a write. If not in memory and memory is full, find the page with the oldest access time to evict. If the evicted page is dirty, increment a disk write counter. Replace the oldest page with the new page, update its access time, and set its dirty bit accordingly. Return the total number of disk writes. Example: given five distinct write requests, returns one disk write.

title: Markdown List Converter
spec: Write a function `convert(lines)` where lines is a list of strings. Strip leading whitespace from every line. If a line starts with a star, replace the star with a number and a dot, incrementing the number for each consecutive item. If a line starts with a dash, leave it but ensure there is exactly one space after the dash. If a line is empty, reset the numbering counter back to one. If a line does not start with a star or dash and is not empty, append it to the previous line separated by a space. If the very first line is regular text, just keep it as is. Return the list of processed strings. Example: given a star and Hello, returns one dot Hello.

title: Pixel Art Hash Visualizer
spec: Write a function `visualize(bytes)` where bytes is a list of integers from zero to two hundred fifty five. Create an empty grid of three by three. Group the bytes into chunks of three. Sum each chunk to get an integer value. Map the sum modulo four to a symbol where zero is a dot, one is a dash, two is a plus, and three is a star. Fill the grid row by row with these symbols. If the bytes list runs out before the grid is full, wrap around to the start of the byte list. Once the grid is full, if any row contains all identical symbols, replace them all with hash marks. Return a list of three strings representing the rows. Example: given all zeros, returns a grid with hash marks.

title: Sports League Standings Calculator
spec: Write a function `rank(matches)` where matches is a list of tuples containing team a name, team a score, team b name, and team b score. Track points, goals for, and goals against for each team. A win awards three points, a tie awards one point, and a loss awards zero. Add the match scores to the respective goals for and goals against totals. Calculate goal difference as goals for minus goals against. Sort the teams primarily by points descending. Sort secondarily by goal difference descending. Sort tertiarily by goals for descending. Sort finally by team name alphabetically. Return a list of team names in the fully ranked order. Example: given Team A scores two and Team B scores one, returns Team A then Team B.

title: Bookstore Pricing Logic
spec: Write a function `price(books)` where books is a list of tuples containing title, category, price, and quantity. Calculate the base cost as price multiplied by quantity. If the category is fiction, apply a ten percent discount to that base cost. If the category is educational and the quantity is three or more, apply a twenty percent discount. Sum all the discounted costs to find the cart total. If this total exceeds fifty, shipping is free, otherwise shipping is a flat five. If the cart has more than ten items in total quantity, apply an additional global five percent off the cart sum before adding shipping. Return a tuple of the final total and the shipping cost, both rounded to two decimal places. Example: given one fiction book at ten, returns nine and five shipping.

title: Thread Scheduler Priority
spec: Write a function `schedule(threads)` where threads is a list of tuples containing thread id, base priority, execution time, and wait time. Give a thread one bonus priority point for every ten units of wait time, simulating aging. Add this bonus to the base priority to compute the effective priority. If the execution time is under five, add two additional points to the effective priority for quick completion. Sort the threads by effective priority in descending order. If effective priorities tie, prefer the thread with the shorter execution time. If they are still tied, prefer the one with the longer wait time. Return a list of thread ids in the order they should run. Example: given thread one with high priority and thread two with low, returns thread one then thread two.

title: Optical Character Post-processor
spec: Write a function `correct(words)` where words is a list of string words generated by a scanner. If a word is entirely uppercase but contains a zero, replace the zero with the letter O. If a word is entirely lowercase but contains a one, replace the one with the letter l. If a word starts with a punctuation mark, strip the mark. If a word ends with multiple punctuation marks, reduce them to a single one. If a word has alternating cases throughout, force the entire word to lowercase. Keep a running count of the total number of changes made across all words. Return a tuple containing the corrected list of words and the change count integer. Example: given HELL0, returns HELLO and a change count of one.

title: Luggage Weight Distributor
spec: Write a function `distribute(bags)` where bags is a list of integer weights. Sort the bags from heaviest to lightest. Maintain two containers starting at zero weight. Iterate through the sorted bags and place the current bag into the container with the lesser current total weight. If the container weights are exactly equal, place the bag into container one. Track the count of bags placed in each container. If a bag weighs more than fifty, skip it entirely because it is too heavy. If adding a bag causes a container to exceed one hundred in total weight, reject the packing and return an empty list. Return a tuple containing the final weight of container one and container two. Example: given weights ten and twenty, returns twenty and ten.

title: Archery Tournament Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(arrows)` to evaluate an archery round. Arrows is a list of string hits. Inner gold is 10, outer gold is 9, red is 8, blue is 6, white is 2. An X counts as 10 points and is tracked separately for tie breaks. A miss is 0. Iterate through the list and keep a running total. If a player scores three consecutive tens of any kind, they get a flat 5 point bonus applied once immediately. If the final total ends in the digit 5, add 1 point to make it even. Return a tuple containing the final total score and the total count of X hits. For example, given an input of X, inner gold, red, blue, the output should be a total of 34 and an X count of 1.

title: Tapas Bill Calculator
spec: Implement `bill(plates, hour)` to compute a restaurant tab. Plates is a list of string pick types. Short red picks are 2 dollars, long blue picks are 3 dollars, flat wooden picks are 5 dollars, and silver picks are 10 dollars. Calculate the base total. If the hour is between 16 and 18 inclusive, apply a 20 percent happy hour discount to the red and blue picks before adding to the total. Groups with over 10 plates total get one red pick for free, so subtract 2 dollars from the total. Add a 10 percent late night surcharge to the final discounted total if the hour is 22 or later. The tip is automatically 15 percent of the absolute base total before any discounts or surcharges. Return a tuple with the final amount to pay and the tip amount, both rounded to two decimal places.

title: Scuba Dive Profile Planner
spec: Create `plan(depth, time)` to calculate diving decompression requirements. Calculate nitrogen load based on depth in meters and bottom time in minutes. Base penalty is depth multiplied by 2. Add the bottom time to the penalty. If depth exceeds 30 meters, double the current penalty. If time exceeds 40 minutes, add a flat 20 to the penalty. If the depth is less than 10 meters, apply a 5 point shallow deduction. If the total penalty is above 100, a decompression stop is required at 5 meters for a duration equal to the penalty minus 100, divided by 2. If the penalty is above 150, add a deep stop at 10 meters for 5 minutes. Return a tuple of the final penalty score, the shallow stop duration, and the deep stop duration.

title: Sailing Regatta Handicap
spec: Write `rank(boats)` to determine race winners. Boats is a list of tuples containing an integer sail number, an integer class rating, and an elapsed time in minutes. The corrected time is elapsed minutes multiplied by 100, then divided by the rating. If the elapsed minutes are under 30, add a 5 minute sprint penalty to the corrected time. If the rating is exactly 100, subtract 2 minutes from the corrected time. If a boat class rating is 0 or negative, it is disqualified and dropped entirely from the results. If the corrected time is greater than 100, add a 10 percent fatigue penalty. Sort the valid boats by corrected time in ascending order. Return a list of the sail numbers representing the final winning order.

title: Curling End Scorer
spec: Implement `evaluate(stones)` to score a round of curling. Stones is a list of tuples with team color as a string, x coordinate, and y coordinate. The center target is at coordinate 0, 0. A stone is only considered in the house if its straight line distance to the center is strictly less than 12 units. Filter out all stones outside the house. Find the team color with the closest stone to the center. That team scores 1 point for every stone they have that is closer to the center than the opponent's absolute closest stone. If the opponent has no stones in the house, the winning team scores all their stones in the house. Return a tuple of the winning color and the integer points scored, or a tie string and 0 if the house is completely empty.

title: Mountain Bike Suspension Tuner
spec: Create `tune(weight, style)` to optimize bicycle shock settings. Weight is in kilograms and style is a string. Base air pressure is weight multiplied by 0.8. Base rebound is 5 clicks and base compression is 3 clicks. If style is aggressive, add 15 to the air pressure, increase rebound clicks by 2, and add 1 to compression. If style is casual, reduce compression by 1 and subtract 5 from air pressure. If weight is over 80, add 1 rebound click for every full 10 kilograms over 80. If weight is under 60, decrease rebound by 1. Air pressure must not exceed 120, and rebound must not fall below 0. Return a list containing the final air pressure, rebound clicks, and compression clicks.

title: Dog Show Judgement
spec: Write `judge(dogs)` to evaluate a competition. Dogs is a list of tuples containing name, integer height, integer weight, and integer coat score. The ideal breed height is 50, and you must subtract 2 points from a base score of 100 for every unit of difference. The ideal weight is 20, subtract 3 points for every unit of difference. Add the coat score directly to the total. If the coat score is 10, add a 5 point perfect grooming bonus. If the weight is strictly over 25, apply a 10 point overweight penalty. If the height is under 40, apply a 5 point stunted penalty. Return the name string of the dog with the highest final total score. Break ties by taking the first dog that appears in the list.

title: Ice Skating Routine Scorer
spec: Implement `score(elements, falls)` to calculate a skater's mark. Elements is a list of float base values for jumps and spins. Falls is an integer. Sum all the base values. The last element in the list always receives a 10 percent bonus to its base value. Deduct 1 point for the first fall, and 1 point for the second fall. Deduct 2 points for each subsequent fall after the second. If the total base value before any deductions exceeds 40, award a flat 3 point presentation bonus. If there are no falls at all, award a 2 point flawless execution bonus. The minimum possible final score is 0. Return the final float score rounded to two decimal places.

title: Woodworking Cut Optimizer
spec: Create `optimize(length, cuts)` to minimize lumber waste. Length is the total available board size as an integer. Cuts is a list of requested piece lengths. Sort the requested cuts in descending order. Greedily assign cuts to the board if they fit in the remaining length. Each successful cut reduces the remaining length by its size. Every successful cut after the first one removes an additional 1 unit of kerf waste from the board length. Count how many cuts could not be accommodated, and sum their total unfulfilled lengths. If the remaining board length at the end is under 5 units, flag it as scrap. Return a tuple containing the number of successful cuts, the unfulfilled length sum, and a boolean indicating if the remainder is scrap.

title: Magic Trick Shuffle Tracker
spec: Write `track(position, moves)` to follow a specific card during a routine. A standard deck has exactly 52 cards, with indices from 0 to 51. Position is the starting index. Moves is a list of string commands. A cut command shifts the index down by 26, wrapping around to the top if it drops below 0. A reverse command subtracts the current index from 51. An out faro shuffle splits the deck in half and interleaves them, which mathematically doubles the index if it is 25 or less, or doubles the index minus 26 and adds 1 if it is greater than 25. Ignore any unrecognized commands. Return the final index of the card after applying all commands in sequence.

title: Tea Steeping Optimizer
spec: Implement `steep(tea, weight)` to brew the perfect cup. Tea is a string type and weight is in grams. The base water temperature is 80 degrees celsius and the base steep time is 120 seconds. If the tea is black, increase the temperature by 15 degrees and the time by 60 seconds. If the tea is green, decrease the temperature by 10 degrees and the time by 30 seconds. If the tea is herbal, set the temperature to 100 degrees and double the base time. If the weight is strictly over 5 grams, add 30 seconds per extra gram. If the weight is under 3 grams, subtract 15 seconds. Return a tuple of the final integer temperature and integer time in seconds.

title: Pottery Firing Schedule
spec: Create `fire(clay, thickness)` to determine kiln timings. Clay is a string type and thickness is in millimeters. The base ramp speed is 200 degrees per hour. The target temperature is 1000 degrees. If the clay is porcelain, the target becomes 1200 degrees. If the clay is earthenware, the target drops to 900 degrees. If the thickness is over 10 millimeters, halve the ramp speed to prevent cracking. Calculate the total hours required to reach the target temperature from 0 degrees. Add a flat 2 hour hold time at the peak temperature. If the clay is porcelain, add a slow cool down phase of 3 hours. Return the total firing schedule time in hours rounded up to the nearest integer.

title: Fencing Bout Referee
spec: Write `referee(actions)` to score a match. Actions is a list of string events like left attack, right parry, left touch, right touch, double touch. Track the current right of way, starting with none. An attack event grants right of way to that side. A parry event transfers right of way to the defender. A touch event scores 1 point for that side only if they currently hold right of way, otherwise no points are scored. A double touch scores 1 point for whichever fencer holds right of way. If an attack occurs while the other side has right of way, the right of way is reset to none. Return a tuple of the left score and right score integers.

title: Astrological Chart Calculator
spec: Implement `chart(month, day)` to find zodiac details. Month is an integer from 1 to 12, day is an integer. Determine the sun sign based on standard monthly date boundaries, for example March 21 starts Aries. Assign the element: fire for Aries Leo Sagittarius, earth for Taurus Virgo Capricorn, air for Gemini Libra Aquarius, water for Cancer Scorpio Pisces. If the day is within 2 days of any sign boundary, set the cusp flag to true. If the month is 2 and the day is 29, set a special leap year flag. Return a tuple containing the sign string, the element string, the boolean cusp flag, and the boolean leap year flag.

title: Perfume Blend Classifier
spec: Create `classify(ingredients)` to categorize a fragrance. Ingredients is a list of tuples containing a scent category string and an integer volume. Calculate the total volume of all ingredients. Find the percentage of floral, woody, citrus, and musk categories relative to the total volume. If floral is strictly over 50 percent, classify as a floral perfume. If woody and citrus together exceed 60 percent, classify as fresh woody. If musk exceeds 30 percent, classify as heavy musk. Otherwise classify as a complex blend. If the total number of distinct ingredients is greater than 5, prepend the word rich to the classification string. Return the final classification string.

title: Geocaching Clue Decoder
spec: Write `decode(clues, offset)` to solve a puzzle. Clues is a list of numeric coordinate strings. Parse each string into an integer. Shift each value by adding the integer offset. If the shifted value is negative, take the absolute value and multiply it by 2. If the shifted value ends in the digit 0, integer divide it by 10. If the shifted value is exactly 42, add a flat 100 point bonus to it. Sum all the final adjusted values together. If the total sum is a multiple of 3, return the sum directly. Otherwise, return the sum plus the remainder of dividing the sum by 3.

title: Meteor Shower Forecaster
spec: Implement `forecast(altitude, moon)` to predict viewing conditions. Altitude is the radiant elevation in degrees above the horizon. Moon is the lunar illumination percentage. The base visible rate is 100 meteors per hour. If the altitude is under 20 degrees, reduce the base rate by 70 percent. If the altitude is between 20 and 50 degrees inclusive, reduce it by 30 percent. Subtract 1 meteor from the rate for every full percent of moon illumination. If the moon is over 80 percent, apply an extra heavy glare penalty of 20 meteors. If the final calculated rate drops below 0, set it to 0. Return the final integer rate.

title: Vinyl Record Grading
spec: Create `grade(scratches, wear)` to appraise an album. Scratches is an integer count and wear is a string condition. The base score is 100 points representing mint condition. Subtract 5 points for each scratch. If scratches exceed 3, subtract an additional 10 points for surface noise. If wear is light, subtract 8 points. If wear is heavy, subtract 20 points. If wear is none and scratches are 0, add a 5 point pristine bonus. If the final score is above 90, return mint. If the score is between 71 and 90 inclusive, return good. If the score is 50 to 70, return fair. Otherwise return poor.

title: Chocolate Tempering Guide
spec: Write `temper(type, mass)` to generate a confectionary schedule. Type is a string of the chocolate variety, mass is in grams. Base melt temperature is 45 degrees, cooling temperature is 27 degrees, and working temperature is 31 degrees. If the type is milk chocolate, reduce all three target temperatures by 2 degrees. If the type is white chocolate, reduce all target temperatures by 4 degrees. The base time at each stage is 10 minutes. If the mass is over 500 grams, add 5 minutes per additional full 100 grams to every stage time. Return a tuple containing the melt temperature, cooling temperature, working temperature, and the stage time in minutes.

title: Knitting Pattern Generator
spec: Implement `pattern(gauge, chest, length)` to calculate yarn requirements. Gauge is stitches per 10 centimeters, chest and length are in centimeters. Calculate total cast on stitches by multiplying chest by gauge and dividing by 10. Add 4 extra stitches for the selvedge edges. Total rows is the length multiplied by the gauge divided by 10. If the total rows calculation results in an odd number, add 1 to make it an even number. Calculate the yardage required by multiplying the total stitches by the total rows, then dividing by 20. Calculate the number of skeins needed by dividing the yardage by 200 and rounding up to the nearest integer. Return a tuple of stitches, rows, and skeins.

title: Origami Crease Pattern Validator
spec: Create `validate(angles, assignments)` to verify a flat foldable vertex. Angles is a list of float degrees in clockwise order around a single point. Assignments is a list of strings, either mountain or valley. The sum of alternating angles must exactly equal 180 degrees to satisfy Kawasaki theorem. The absolute difference between the count of mountain folds and valley folds must be exactly 2 to satisfy Maekawa theorem. All angles must be strictly greater than 0. The total sum of all angles must be exactly 360 degrees. Return a boolean true if all these conditions are strictly met, otherwise return false.

title: Wine Fermentation Monitor
spec: Write `monitor(sugar, temp)` to check brewing health. Sugar is a list of daily gravity readings as floats. Temp is the current liquid temperature in celsius. If the sugar list has at least 3 readings and the last 3 values are identical, the fermentation is stuck. If the temperature exceeds 30 degrees, yeast stress is high and cooling is required. If the last sugar reading drops below 0.99, the fermentation is complete. Determine the current status string by prioritizing complete, then stuck, then cooling needed, and finally active if none apply. Return a tuple of the status string and the total drop in sugar from the first to the last reading.

title: Fireworks Display Sequence
spec: Implement `sequence(beats, delay)` to synchronize a pyrotechnic show. Beats is a list of integer timestamps in milliseconds. Delay is the fuse burn time in milliseconds. Subtract the delay from each beat to calculate the required launch time. If a calculated launch time is strictly negative, drop that firework from the schedule. Iterate through the launch times; if two consecutive launch times are within 50 milliseconds of each other, merge them into a single launch time by taking their integer average. Repeat this merge until no two launch times are within 50 milliseconds. Return the final list of adjusted launch times sorted in ascending order.

title: Haunted House Scare Trigger
spec: Create `trigger(sensors, panic)` to control attraction animatronics. Sensors is a list of boolean values indicating motion detection in consecutive rooms. Panic is the current average heart rate of the guests. If panic is above 120, immediately return a safe mode string to disable all jump scares. If sensors indicate motion in 3 consecutive rooms, return a chase event string. If only the last room in the list has motion and all others are false, return a finale event string. If no motion is detected anywhere, return a reset string. If none of the specific event conditions are met, return a wait string.

title: Bonsai Watering Schedule
spec: Write `water(species, humidity, temp)` to maintain miniature trees. Species is a string, humidity is a percentage, temp is in celsius. The base watering interval is 3 days. If the species is pine or juniper, add 2 days to the interval. If the species is maple, subtract 1 day. If the ambient humidity is below 40 percent, subtract 1 day. If the temperature is strictly above 25 degrees, subtract another day. If the temperature is below 10 degrees, add 1 day. If the final calculated interval drops below 1 day, force it to 1 day. If the interval is over 5 days, cap it at a maximum of 5 days. Return the final integer interval in days.

title: Space Debris Collision Evader
spec: Analyzes whether orbital satellites are at risk of colliding with space junk over several future time steps via `evade(satellites, debris)`. The logic must simulate the positions of both satellites and debris using their current coordinates and velocity vectors. For each time step, calculate the Euclidean distance between every satellite and piece of debris. If the distance falls below the sum of their physical radii, an evasion maneuver is required. Determine a safe thrust direction for the satellite that avoids all nearby debris paths. Return a list of evasion vectors for the endangered satellites. For example, given satellites [(0, 0, 2)] and debris [(5, 0, 1, -1, 0)], it returns a list like [(0, 1)].

title: Ant Pheromone Trail Updater
spec: Simulates the decay and reinforcement of chemical trails left by ants navigating a grid using `update(trails, ants)`. First, decrease the pheromone concentration in every grid cell by a universal evaporation rate to model time passing. Next, iterate over the positions of all active ants. Increase the trail strength significantly if an ant is returning with food, and slightly if the ant is merely exploring. Ensure no cell exceeds a maximum saturation limit to prevent runaway accumulation. Return the final grid of pheromone concentrations. For example, a 2x2 grid [[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]] with a foraging ant at 0,1 might become [[0.9, 0.5], [0.0, 0.0]].

title: Submarine Sonar Ping Analyzer
spec: Processes acoustic signals to detect underwater obstacles and vessels through `analyze(pings, echoes)`. The logic correlates emitted sonar pulses with received sound echoes by matching their frequency profiles. Calculate the distance to the target based on the time delay and the speed of sound in seawater. Ignore any echoes that return almost instantaneously or extremely late, as they represent surface clutter or deep ocean noise. Categorize valid targets as small, medium, or large based on the decibel strength of the returning echo. Return the identified targets with their classifications and ranges. Example input of pings [(0.0, 400)] and echoes [(2.0, 400, 85)] outputs [("large", 1500.0)].

title: Avalanche Risk Assessor
spec: Evaluates the danger level of mountain terrain based on topography and recent weather patterns via `assess(slopes, snowfall)`. Analyze each slope by first checking its steepness, as angles between thirty and forty five degrees are the most prone to sliding. Increase the hazard score if the recent snowfall exceeds a critical depth or if the underlying base layer is known to be weak. If the terrain is heavily forested, apply a slight reduction to the risk score due to tree anchoring. Classify slopes exceeding a specific threshold as extreme danger zones. Return a list of risk categories for the evaluated areas. For instance, an input of slope 38 degrees with 50cm snowfall returns ["extreme"].

title: River Sediment Deposition
spec: Models the geological process of a river eroding and building up its bed over time using `deposit(flow, terrain)`. The river begins with a certain carrying capacity for suspended sediment based on its water velocity. As the river traverses different elevation points, adjust its velocity according to the steepness of the gradient. In flat areas where the water slows, deposit a fraction of the carried sediment, increasing the terrain elevation. In steep rapids, erode the riverbed, decreasing elevation and adding material to the suspended load. Return the updated elevation profile of the riverbed. For example, given terrain [10, 8, 8, 4], the output might be [9.8, 8.2, 7.8, 4.0].

title: Sourdough Starter Feeder
spec: Calculates the growth and maintenance schedule of a fermentation culture over several days via `feed(starter, temperatures)`. The daily volume expansion of the culture depends heavily on the ambient room temperature, with warmer conditions causing rapid doubling. Before adding daily flour and water, check if the current volume plus the new ingredients will exceed the jar capacity. If an overflow is imminent, discard exactly half of the active culture to make room. Accumulate the total amount of discarded material over the observation period. Return the final active volume and the total discarded amount. For example, starting with 100g at 25C for 3 days might return (150, 200).

title: Bird Migration Router
spec: Determines optimal resting locations for migrating birds travelling long distances through `route(flock, wetlands)`. The birds possess a maximum daily flight range before they require food and rest. Evaluate a sequence of potential wetland coordinates to find the furthest possible stopover within this range. Skip any locations that have dried up or lack sufficient food resources. If a massive body of water prevents reaching a safe resting spot, the flock must alter its path to skirt the obstacle. Return the sequence of selected stopover coordinates. Given range 100 and wetlands at [50, 90, 150, 180], it returns [90, 180].

title: Highway Toll Plaza Router
spec: Directs incoming traffic to the appropriate toll booths based on vehicle classification and current congestion using `assign(vehicles, lanes)`. Heavy trucks must be routed exclusively to reinforced, wide lanes designed for commercial transport. Emergency vehicles bypass the queue entirely by taking a dedicated open lane. Standard passenger cars evaluate all available standard lanes and enter the one with the fewest waiting vehicles. Update the vehicle count for the chosen lane to ensure subsequent routing remains balanced. Return the assigned lane numbers for the sequence of arriving vehicles. For inputs ["car", "truck", "car"] and 3 lanes, output could be [0, 2, 1].

title: Wind Turbine Blade Adjuster
spec: Optimizes the rotational efficiency and safety of a wind farm based on meteorological data via `pitch(wind, turbines)`. First, compare the current wind speed to the minimum required threshold, shutting down turbines if the breeze is too weak. For operational speeds, calculate the ideal blade angle to extract maximum aerodynamic energy. If an extreme gale is detected, immediately feather all blades to be parallel with the wind direction to prevent structural damage. Log any turbines that require maintenance due to excessive vibration during high winds. Return the newly calculated blade angles for the entire array. Example: wind speed 25m/s returns [90.0, 90.0, 90.0] for three turbines.

title: Brewery Fermentation Monitor
spec: Evaluates the progress of alcoholic fermentation using periodic specific gravity and temperature measurements with `monitor(batches, readings)`. Calculate the current alcohol content by determining the difference between the initial starting gravity and the latest measurement. If the liquid temperature rises above the yeast tolerance limit, trigger a cooling jacket alert to prevent off flavors. Identify batches where the specific gravity has remained identical for three consecutive days, signaling that the yeast has consumed all available sugars. Return a list of statuses indicating whether each batch is active, cooling, or finished. Example: a stable gravity of 1.010 for three readings returns ["finished"].

title: Coffee Roasting Profile
spec: Tracks the thermal development of coffee beans during the roasting process over a series of time intervals via `roast(beans, temperatures)`. Identify the end of the initial drying phase when the bean mass temperature begins to rise rapidly. Pinpoint the occurrence of first crack, an audible popping stage indicating a light roast, when the temperature hits a specific elevated threshold. Monitor the development time following first crack, as extending this phase creates a darker flavor profile. Terminate the process before second crack to avoid burning the batch. Return the final roast classification and total development time. Given temperatures [150, 205, 215, 220], output is ("medium", 2).

title: Mushroom Toxicity Classifier
spec: Evaluates physical characteristics of foraged fungi to separate edible varieties from deadly ones using `classify(specimens, features)`. Analyze the combination of cap shape, gill structure, and spore color for each specimen. Immediately flag any mushroom possessing both a bulbous base and a prominent ring on the stem, as these are hallmarks of highly toxic species. Specimens with bright red caps and white spots should also be rejected regardless of other features. Accept mushrooms with spongy pores instead of gills, provided their flesh does not stain blue when bruised. Return a safety verdict for each analyzed specimen. Example: [("red", "white spots", "gills")] returns ["poisonous"].

title: Gemstone Yield Calculator
spec: Estimates the final faceted carat weight obtained from raw crystalline minerals via `calculate(rough, cuts)`. Different cutting styles require different amounts of raw material; round brilliant cuts sacrifice a significant portion of the stone to achieve maximum light reflection. Step cuts like emerald shapes preserve more original mass but demand flawless internal clarity. Inspect the raw stone data for internal fractures, applying a percentage penalty to the final weight if imperfections must be cut away. Return the projected final carat weight and the estimated waste percentage. Example: rough 10 carats and cut "round" might return (4.5, 55.0).

title: Coral Reef Bleaching Tracker
spec: Assesses the health of marine ecosystems by monitoring thermal stress over a continuous period using `track(reefs, temperatures)`. Calculate the weekly temperature anomalies by comparing current ocean surface temperatures to historical summer maximums. Accumulate these anomalies to determine the degree heating weeks for each reef location. If the accumulated stress surpasses a critical threshold, the corals will expel their symbiotic algae, resulting in severe bleaching. Mark reefs that experience sudden temperature drops as recovering. Return the current stress level and bleaching status for every monitored location. Given anomalies [1, 2, 1, 0.5] over weeks, output could be (4.5, "warning").

title: Tectonic Plate Boundary Simulator
spec: Models the geological consequences of continental and oceanic crusts shifting against one another via `collide(plates, vectors)`. When two continental masses converge, calculate the height of the resulting mountain range based on their combined momentum. If a dense oceanic plate collides with a lighter continental plate, model a subduction zone that generates a deep ocean trench and volcanic activity. When plates move apart in a divergent boundary, simulate the creation of new crust from upwelling magma. Return a description of the resulting geological formations and their estimated scale. Example: plates ["oceanic", "continental"] converging at 5cm/yr returns [("trench", 8000)].

title: Dinosaur Fossil Assembler
spec: Reconstructs ancient skeletal structures by matching excavated bone fragments to known biological templates with `assemble(bones, anatomy)`. Iterate through the discovered fossils, sorting them into categories like vertebrae, ribs, and cranial fragments. When multiple bones fit the same skeletal position, prioritize the best preserved piece and relegate the others to an alternate display. Calculate the overall completeness of the skeleton by checking off mandatory structural components. If the skull or major leg bones are absent, flag the display as requiring synthetic cast replacements. Return the completion percentage and a list of missing vital elements. Example input of just a femur and ribs returns (25.0, ["skull", "pelvis"]).

title: Lighthouse Visibility Range
spec: Determines which navigational beacons are visible to vessels traversing coastal waters at night using `illuminate(lighthouses, ships)`. Establish the maximum geographical range of each lighthouse by factoring in the curvature of the earth and the elevation of the light source. Reduce this theoretical range if the current weather conditions involve heavy fog or precipitation. Calculate the direct line of sight distance between every vessel and nearby coastal structures. Return a mapping of each ship to the list of lighthouses currently shining within its visible horizon. For instance, ship at distance 10km from a 15km range lighthouse returns [[0]].

title: Glacier Melt Runoff
spec: Predicts the seasonal volume of freshwater generated by retreating mountain ice fields via `melt(glaciers, climate)`. Compute the baseline melting rate using the surface area of the ice and average daily solar radiation. Increase the expected runoff if wind storms have deposited dark soot or dust on the glacier, lowering its reflectivity. Conversely, pause the melting calculations for days when fresh snowfall covers the ice, insulating it from the sun. Sum the daily water production to determine the overall seasonal output. Return the total projected volume of glacial runoff. Example: 10 square kilometers with 5 sunny days and 1 snowy day might return 50000.0.

title: Volcanic Ash Plume Predictor
spec: Models the atmospheric dispersion of hazardous particulates following a seismic eruption with `predict(eruptions, winds)`. Determine the initial vertical height of the ash column based on the explosive energy and duration of the geological event. Calculate the horizontal drift of the cloud by analyzing prevailing upper atmospheric wind currents. Simulate the gradual fallout of heavier rock particles, which causes the dense core of the plume to shrink as it travels away from the source. Return the final coordinates of the airborne hazard zone and its estimated particulate density. For an eruption at 0,0 with eastward wind, the output could be (100, 0, "high").

title: Radio Telescope Interference Filter
spec: Processes astronomical data streams to isolate genuine cosmic phenomena from local earthly noise via `filter(signals, sources)`. Scan the raw frequency data for prominent amplitude spikes indicating a strong transmission. Cross reference these spikes against a database of known terrestrial emitters, such as orbiting communication satellites and radar stations. If a detected frequency closely aligns with human technology, mathematically subtract its waveform from the raw data stream. Preserve and highlight any remaining unexplained signals that originate from deep space. Return the sanitized data array ready for scientific analysis. Example: signal [1420.4, 2400.0] and source [2400.0] returns [1420.4].

title: Orchid Greenhouse Climate Controller
spec: Manages environmental conditions to cultivate rare flowering plants with specific atmospheric requirements using `regulate(orchids, sensors)`. Monitor the ambient humidity sensors, activating the automated misting system if the air becomes too dry for tropical species. Evaluate daytime sunlight intensity, deploying shade cloths if the greenhouse becomes dangerously hot, or turning on artificial grow lights during heavy cloud cover. Initiate a deliberate temperature drop during the night cycle to simulate natural conditions and encourage blossom development. Return the list of hardware commands issued to climate control mechanisms. Given low humidity and high temp, output is ["mist_on", "shade_on"].

title: Ski Chairlift Loading Optimizer
spec: Organizes waiting winter sports enthusiasts onto aerial lift equipment to minimize queue times via `load(skiers, chairs)`. Process groups of skiers based on their desired party size, attempting to keep friends and family seated together. If a group occupies fewer seats than the maximum capacity of a chair, pull individuals from the dedicated singles line to fill the empty spots. When a massive group exceeds a single chair's capacity, divide them evenly across consecutive moving seats. Return the organized sequence of passenger assignments for the departing chairs. For a 4-person chair and groups [3, 2, 1], output is [[3, 1], [2]].

title: Hot Air Balloon Flight Physics
spec: Calculates the vertical trajectory of an aerostat based on thermal buoyancy and atmospheric drag with `ascend(balloon, atmosphere)`. Simulate the pilot activating the propane burner, which raises the internal envelope temperature and generates upward lift. Account for the decreasing density of the surrounding air as the balloon climbs, which naturally diminishes the lifting force at higher altitudes. Automatically trigger short maintenance burns if the descent rate becomes dangerously rapid due to cooling internal air. Return the logged altitude measurements over the duration of the flight. Example: firing burner for 2 minutes might yield altitudes [0, 50, 120, 110].

title: Juggling Cascade Validator
spec: Verifies whether a sequence of airborne object manipulations forms a sustainable physical pattern using `validate(throws, hands)`. Analyze each throw in the sequence, using its height value to determine exactly how many beats it will remain suspended in the air. Calculate the future landing time for every object to predict which hand will receive it. Ensure that no two objects are scheduled to land in the same hand simultaneously, as this results in an unavoidable collision and pattern drop. Return a boolean confirming the pattern's validity and the timestamps of any detected collisions. Sequence of heights [3, 3, 3] returns (True, []).

title: Mars Rover Sample Collector
spec: Prioritizes geological specimens for a robotic explorer to gather before its energy reserves are depleted via `collect(rocks, battery)`. Evaluate a field of potential targets by comparing their scientific importance, physical mass, and distance from the landing site. Deduct battery power for every meter traveled and apply an additional energy cost based on the density of the rock when using the core drill. Select a path that maximizes the total scientific value acquired without dropping the power levels below the threshold needed to transmit data back to orbit. Return the catalog of acquired specimens and the final battery percentage. Example: rocks at various distances might return (["basalt", "hematite"], 15.5).

title: Camera Film Developer
spec: Write a function `develop(rolls)` that calculates film processing times. The input is a list of tuples containing film format, base iso rating, shot iso rating, developer temperature in celsius, and film grain type. Calculate push or pull stops by comparing shot iso to base iso, and set the base developer time to ten minutes at twenty degrees celsius. Adjust this time by changing it ten percent per degree of difference from twenty, then add fifteen percent to the time per push stop or subtract ten percent per pull stop. Stop bath is a constant one minute, while fixer time is five minutes for standard grain or eight minutes for tabular grain. Wash time is exactly double the fixer time, and a final rinse of thirty seconds is added if the format is large. Return a list of total processing times in minutes for each roll, for example input [("large", 400, 800, 22, "standard")] yields [24.5].

title: Glassblowing Annealer
spec: Write a function `anneal(pieces)` that computes cooling schedules for glass. The input is a list of tuples with piece thickness in millimeters and glass type as a string. Heating time in minutes is the thickness squared multiplied by two, while soak time is thirty minutes base plus five minutes per millimeter of thickness. Fast cooling drops temperature rapidly and takes twenty minutes for soft glass or thirty for hard glass, whereas slow cooling takes the thickness multiplied by ten minutes. If the piece is thicker than fifty millimeters, add an extra twenty percent time to the slow cool phase to prevent thermal shock cracking.
