Calculate the total cycle time for each piece and return a tuple containing the longest cycle time needed for the batch alongside the average cycle time. For example, an input of [(40, "soft")] returns a maximum and average time of 3850.0 minutes.

title: Beekeeping Honey Extractor
spec: Write a function `extract(frames)` that simulates processing beehive frames. The input is a list of tuples containing capped percentage as an integer, raw weight in pounds, and nectar type. First, discard any frames that are less than seventy percent capped, then calculate uncapping time which takes two minutes plus one minute for every ten percent over the seventy percent threshold. Spinning time starts at a base of five minutes, but clover nectar adds two minutes and wildflower adds four. Extracted honey volume is the raw weight multiplied by the capped percentage divided by one hundred, minus a ten percent wax loss, and filtering takes three minutes per extracted pound. Return a tuple of the total extracted honey volume and total processing time in minutes for the valid frames. For input [(80, 10, "clover")], it returns (7.2, 31.6).

title: Textile Weaving Setup
spec: Write a function `weave(patterns)` that estimates loom production time. The input is a list of tuples containing fabric length in meters, thread count per meter, and a complexity level string. Warp threads equal the thread count multiplied by fifty, while weft threads are the length multiplied by the thread count. Tension setup takes thirty minutes base, but a high complexity pattern adds forty five minutes to this setup time. Base weaving speed is one hundred threads inserted per minute, though medium complexity reduces this speed by twenty percent and high complexity reduces it by forty percent. Calculate the total threads used per pattern and total machine time in hours, returning a list of tuples containing total threads and total hours for each pattern. Example input [(10, 200, "medium")] produces [(3000, 1.0)].

title: Soil Nutrient Scorer
spec: Write a function `analyze(samples)` to evaluate agricultural soil tests. The input is a list of tuples with ph level, nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels as integers. The ideal ph is between six and seven inclusive, adding a penalty score of ten for every point outside this range. The ideal nitrogen level is fifty, phosphorus is thirty, and potassium is forty, so calculate the absolute difference for each nutrient from its ideal value. Double the penalty for any nitrogen deficiencies below fifty and sum all penalties into a total score. A total penalty under twenty is optimal, under fifty is acceptable, and anything above is poor, returning a list of these string categories for each sample. For input [(5, 40, 30, 40)], the penalty is 10 for ph and 20 for nitrogen, returning ["acceptable"].

title: Violin Acoustic Tuning
spec: Write a function `tune(strings)` to calculate adjustments for string instruments. The input is a list of tuples with current frequency, target frequency, and string material string. Calculate the frequency difference for each string, then find the tension adjustment by multiplying this difference by a material constant: steel is zero point five, gut is zero point eight, and synthetic is zero point six. If the difference is greater than ten hertz, add a bridge adjustment warning string to a separate warnings list. Furthermore, if all strings in the input need a frequency increase, add a soundpost warning string to the warnings list. Return a tuple containing the list of tension adjustments and the list of warnings. Example input [(430, 440, "steel")] returns a tuple of ([5.0], ["soundpost warning"]).

title: Bicycle Gearing Analyzer
spec: Write a function `gearing(components)` to calculate bike speeds. The input is a tuple containing a list of chainring teeth counts, a list of cog teeth counts, and the wheel circumference in millimeters. For every combination of chainring and cog, divide the chainring size by the cog size to get the gear ratio, then multiply this ratio by the circumference to get the rollout length in meters. Calculate the speed in kilometers per hour assuming a pedaling cadence of ninety revolutions per minute. Filter out any cross chain combinations, which are defined strictly as the smallest chainring with the smallest cog, or the largest chainring with the largest cog. Return a sorted list of unique speeds rounded to one decimal place. Given input ([30, 50], [15, 20], 2100), the combinations of 50 with 20 and 30 with 15 are ignored.

title: Leather Tanning Stages
spec: Write a function `tan(hides)` to estimate processing times for leather. The input is a list of tuples with animal type, weight in kilograms, and thickness in millimeters. Soaking takes one day per five millimeters of thickness, while liming takes two days for cow, three for buffalo, and one for sheep. Bating time is the weight divided by ten in days, pickling requires a constant two days for all hides, and tanning takes three days plus one extra day for every ten kilograms of weight over twenty. Sum the days for each stage to find the total, and if the total exceeds fifteen days, apply a special preservative treatment which adds two more days. Return a list of the total processing days for each hide. For input [("cow", 30, 10)], the days are 2, 2, 3, 2, 4, totaling 13 days.

title: Seismograph Magnitude Estimator
spec: Write a function `magnitude(events)` to interpret earthquake data. The input is a list of tuples containing primary wave arrival time in seconds, secondary wave arrival time in seconds, and peak amplitude in millimeters. Calculate the time difference between secondary and primary waves, then multiply this difference by eight to estimate the epicenter distance in kilometers. If the distance is under one hundred kilometers, add a local crust modifier of zero point five to the peak amplitude. Calculate the magnitude as the base ten logarithm of the amplitude, plus three times the base ten logarithm of the distance, minus two point nine, setting it to zero if the result is negative. Return a list of tuples containing the estimated distance and the final magnitude rounded to two decimals. For example, input of [(10, 20, 50)] returns [(80, 3.3)].

title: Telescope Lens Alignment
spec: Write a function `align(lenses)` to correct optical aberrations. The input is a list of tuples with focal length in millimeters, current spacing to the next lens, and lens shape string. The ideal spacing between consecutive lenses is the sum of their focal lengths, so calculate the error between current spacing and ideal spacing. If the leading lens is concave, add a dispersion offset of two millimeters to the error, and if the trailing lens is convex, subtract one millimeter from the error. Compute a correction factor which is exactly half of the adjusted error, then sum the absolute values of all correction factors across the array. Return a tuple containing the list of individual correction factors and their total absolute sum. For input [(50, 100, "concave"), (50, 0, "flat")], the correction factors could be [24.0, 0.0].

title: Paint Color Matcher
spec: Write a function `mix(targets)` to calculate paint formulas. The input is a list of target red, green, and blue integer tuples. For each target, find the maximum color component to determine the dominant base pigment, where a red base requires two drops of red pigment per point of red value, green requires three drops per point, and blue requires one drop per point. If the sum of all three components is under two hundred, the color is dark and requires ten drops of thinner, but if the sum is over six hundred it is light and requires twenty drops of white base. Calculate the total drops of each pigment, thinner, and white base needed across all targets. Return a tuple of these five totals in the order of red, green, blue, thinner, and white. Example input [(100, 50, 20)] returns (200, 0, 0, 10, 0).

title: Bread Dough Scoring
spec: Write a function `score(loaves)` to determine baking cuts. The input is a list of tuples with hydration percentage, proofing time in hours, and flour type string. The base cut depth is ten millimeters and the base angle is forty five degrees, but if hydration is over eighty percent, reduce depth by three millimeters and angle by fifteen degrees. If proofing time exceeds twelve hours, increase depth by two millimeters but reduce the angle to zero degrees. Rye flour makes dough extremely sticky, requiring an extra two millimeters of depth and a straight ninety degree angle, which overrides previous angle calculations. Whole wheat requires a shallow five millimeter depth, overriding all other depth rules. Return a list of tuples with the final depth and angle for each loaf, where input [(85, 10, "wheat")] yields [(5, 30)].

title: Watch Escapement Physics
spec: Write a function `escapement(movements)` to evaluate mechanical watch designs. The input is a list of tuples with mainspring torque, balance wheel mass, and beat rate. The base energy is the torque multiplied by ten, while kinetic energy is the mass multiplied by the square of the beat rate, all divided by two. Calculate the transfer efficiency as kinetic energy divided by base energy, then remove five percent of efficiency for every one thousand beat rate units over twenty eight thousand to account for friction. If the final efficiency drops below zero point four, the movement will stall. Calculate power reserve as torque divided by the friction loss percentage, capped at a maximum of seventy two hours. Return a list of tuples containing the power reserve and a boolean indicating if it stalls, with input [(50, 2, 28000)] yielding [(50.0, False)].

title: Rope Knot Strength Evaluator
spec: Write a function `strength(lines)` to calculate load limits. The input is a list of tuples with rope diameter in millimeters, material string, and knot type string. Base strength is the diameter squared multiplied by fifty pounds, with nylon material adding a twenty percent bonus, polyester adding ten percent, and polypropylene subtracting five percent. A bowline knot reduces the final strength by thirty percent, a figure eight knot reduces it by twenty percent, and a square knot reduces it by half. Calculate the breaking strength after all modifiers, and if the final strength falls below one hundred pounds, mark the line as unsafe. Return a tuple containing the list of calculated strengths and an integer count of unsafe lines. Example input [(10, "nylon", "square")] returns a tuple of ([3000.0], 0).

title: Drum Machine Sequencer
spec: Write a function `sequence(hits)` to apply groove to a drum pattern. The input is a list of tuples with step number, instrument name, and base velocity. The sequencer loops through a standard sixteen step bar, and if a hit falls on an even step number, delay its timing by ten percent of a step to create a swing feel. If the instrument is a kick drum on the first step, increase its velocity by twenty, whereas a snare on the fifth or thirteenth step gets a velocity increase of fifteen. Closed hi-hats on off beats get their velocity reduced by ten to create dynamics, then all final velocities are capped at a maximum of one hundred and twenty seven. Return a list of tuples with modified timing offsets and final velocities. Example input [(1, "kick", 100)] returns [(0.0, 120)].

title: Cheese Aging Process
spec: Write a function `age(batches)` to determine maturation schedules. The input is a list of tuples with milk type string, initial moisture percent, and target style string. Base aging time is four weeks, where cow milk adds two weeks, sheep adds four, and goat adds one week, but if the initial moisture is above fifty percent, reduce the total time by two weeks. For a cheddar style, multiply the total time by two and set the target humidity to eighty percent, while brie halves the total time and sets humidity to ninety. For parmesan, multiply the time by four and set humidity to seventy, capping the maximum aging time at two hundred weeks for all styles. Return a list of tuples containing the target weeks and humidity for each batch. For input [("cow", 60, "brie")], it returns [(2.0, 90)].

title: Bookbinding Layout Planner
spec: Write a function `bind(manuscripts)` to plan book printing. The input is a list of tuples containing total page counts and paper weights in grams. A standard signature contains sixteen pages, so divide the page count by sixteen to get the number of full signatures, and if there is a remainder, add blank pages to complete a final full signature. Spine thickness in millimeters is the total pages including blanks multiplied by the paper weight, then divided by twenty thousand. If the thickness exceeds fifty millimeters, split the book into two equal volumes. Return a list of tuples containing the number of signatures, blank pages added, spine thickness, and volume count for each manuscript. Example input [(30, 100)] returns [(2, 2, 0.16, 1)].

title: Freight Train Assembly
spec: Write a function `assemble(cars)` to configure railway transport. The input is a tuple containing a list of car weights in tons and a locomotive power rating integer. Sum the weight of all cars, and since a single locomotive can pull its power rating times fifty in tons, divide the total weight by this capacity to find the number of locomotives needed, rounding up. Base braking distance is the total weight divided by ten in meters, but if more than three locomotives are used, add twenty percent to the braking distance due to extra momentum. If the train exceeds five thousand tons, limit the maximum speed to eighty kilometers per hour, otherwise it is one hundred. Return a tuple of locomotives needed, braking distance, and maximum speed. For input ([500, 500], 20), it returns (1, 100, 100).

title: Water Park Slide Physics
spec: Write a function `slide(riders)` to simulate hydrodynamics. The input is a list of tuples with rider weight in kilograms, height in centimeters, and mat type string. Base speed is twenty meters per second, adding one meter per second for every ten kilograms of weight over fifty, while foam mats increase the speed by ten percent and plastic mats increase it by twenty percent. If the calculated speed exceeds thirty, apply a water brake reduction of five meters per second, then calculate splash length in meters as the speed squared divided by ten. If a rider's height is under one hundred twenty centimeters, restrict them from riding entirely by excluding them from the output. Return a list of tuples containing final speeds and splash lengths for the valid riders. For input [(60, 150, "foam")], returns [(23.1, 53.36)].

title: Language Translation Rules
spec: Write a function `translate(words)` that applies phonetic rules to a list of strings. Process each word individually by first checking if it starts with a vowel, in which case append a standard suffix of yay. If it starts with a consonant, move all leading consonants to the end of the word and append ay. If the original word ends with a double letter, remove one of the duplicate letters before applying any other rules, and if the word contains the letter x anywhere, replace it with the sequence ks immediately at the start of processing. Finally, capitalize the first letter of the resulting word and make all other letters lowercase. Return the list of fully translated words, where an input containing apple and box returns a list with Appleyay and Boksay.

title: Flower Crossbreeding Predictor
spec: Write a function `cross(pairs)` to evaluate inheritance patterns. The input is a list of tuples containing two parent genotype strings of four characters each. For each pair, generate all sixteen combinations by pairing each character of the first parent with each character of the second parent in sequence. Count how many combinations have at least one dominant capital letter for the first trait, and count how many have two recessive lowercase letters for the second trait. A combination is fully dominant if both traits have at least one capital letter, so calculate the percentage of fully dominant offspring out of the sixteen possibilities. Return a list of tuples containing the fully dominant percentage and the count of fully recessive second traits for each pair. For input [("AaBb", "aabb")], it returns [(25.0, 8)].

title: Weather Balloon Data Cleaner
spec: Write a function `clean(readings)` to sanitize atmospheric data. The input is a list of tuples with timestamp in seconds, sensor voltage, and an error code integer. First, remove any readings where the error code is not zero. Then, check the time difference between consecutive remaining readings, and if a gap is exactly two seconds, insert a new interpolated reading with the average voltage of its immediate neighbors. Convert all sensor readings from raw voltage to celsius temperature by multiplying by five and subtracting fifty. If any resulting temperature exceeds one hundred degrees, cap it at one hundred. Return a list of tuples containing the processed timestamps and temperatures, where input [(1, 10, 0), (3, 20, 0)] yields processed temperatures at seconds 1, 2, and 3.

title: Sailboat Rigging Tension
spec: Write a function `rigging(masts)` to calculate standing rigging loads. The input is a list of tuples with mast height in meters, wind speed in knots, and sail area in square meters. Base forestay tension is the mast height multiplied by fifty, and base backstay tension is equal to the forestay. If wind speed is over fifteen knots, increase the backstay tension by twenty percent to depower the main sail, and if sail area is over forty square meters, add ten percent to both stays. Shroud tension is always calculated as exactly half of the backstay tension, but if total tension across all wires exceeds two thousand, reduce all values proportionally to meet the maximum limit. Return a list of tuples containing the forestay, backstay, and shroud tension for each mast. Example input [(10, 20, 50)] returns the adjusted tensions.
